The moral of the story is that it's better to work together and listen to others, instead of being bossy and telling others what to do.

Later, at home, Lucy tried to escape to her room with the orange. But her mom saw her and asked, "What is that in your bag?" Lucy showed her mom the orange and said, "I took it from the store." Her mom was not happy. She told Lucy, "Taking things without asking is wrong. We must go back to the store and say sorry."

Lucy felt bad and learned that taking things without asking is not right. From that day on, she always asked before taking anything.

Her mom smiled and said, "Don't be scared, Lucy. The mailbox is our friend. It brings us letters and surprises from far away." But Lucy still felt scared and didn't want to go near it. Her mom insisted, "Let's go together and see what's inside the mailbox."

The next day, Lucy and her mom walked to the mailbox. Lucy held her mom's hand tight. When they opened the mailbox, they found a big, colorful envelope. Lucy's mom said, "See, Lucy? The mailbox brought us a surprise! Let's take it home and open it together."

Lucy started to feel less scared of the mailbox. She helped her mom carry the envelope home. When they opened it, they found a beautiful card from Lucy's grandma. Lucy was so happy to get a surprise from the mailbox.

From that day on, Lucy was not scared of the mailbox anymore. She even looked forward to checking it with her mom every day. And sometimes, the mailbox would bring her more surprises and make her smile.

Sam looked at Sally and said, "I will help you find your way home." They walked and talked together. Sam held the acorn in one hand and helped Sally with the other. They became good friends.

They all played together under the big green tree. They laughed and sang songs. The bird flew high with his wings, and the squirrel climbed the tree. They were all so happy to celebrate the big red balloon. And they played until the sun went down.

They both went on a long walk to find the treasure. Along the way, they met a big dog named Max. Max wanted the treasure too, and he tried to take the map from Tom.

Tom was scared, but Sue had an idea. "Max, if you help us find the treasure, we can share it with you." Max agreed, and they all continued on their journey. They found the treasure under a big tree. The treasure was a big box of toys that could help them improve their playtime. Tom, Sue, and Max were all very happy and became good friends. They learned that sharing and working together can make things better for everyone.

"Come on, Timmy. It will be fun!" they said.

Lily was scared, but she remembered that she had seen a broomstick nearby. She quickly grabbed it and gave it to the witch. The witch was happy and thanked Lily for her kindness. From that day on, the witch and Lily became friends and played together often.

One day, a goose went to the pond to swim and play. He saw a big bucket near the water. He was curious and wanted to see what was inside. He walked to the bucket and looked in. It was empty.

The goose had an idea. He wanted to fill the bucket with water. He thought it would be fun to splash and make bubbles. He used his beak to scoop up some water and pour it into the bucket. He did it again and again, until the bucket was full.

But the bucket was too heavy for the goose to lift. He tried to push it with his feet, but it did not move. He tried to pull it with his neck, but it did not budge. He was stuck with the bucket.

He started to honk and flap his wings. He hoped someone would hear him and help him. He saw some ducks swimming by. They heard his honks and came to see what was wrong. They saw the goose and the bucket. They laughed and quacked.

"Look at the silly goose!" they said. "He filled the bucket with water and now he can't get rid of it!"

The goose felt sad and angry. He did not like the ducks laughing at him. He wished he had never filled the bucket.

Then he saw a fox sneaking behind the bushes. The fox had a thick fur and a long tail. He had sharp teeth and claws. He liked to eat ducks and geese. He saw the goose and the bucket. He licked his lips and smiled.

"Look at the tasty goose!" he said. "He filled the bucket with water and now he can't run away!"

The goose felt scared and sorry. He did not want the fox to eat him. He wished he had never seen the bucket.

But then he had an idea. He waited for the fox to come closer. He pretended to be weak and helpless. He honked and flapped his wings. He made the water splash and the bucket shake.

The fox thought the goose was easy to catch. He jumped out of the bushes and ran to the bucket. He opened his mouth and reached for the goose.

But the goose was ready. He used his beak to tip the bucket over. The water poured out and hit the fox. The water was cold and wet. The fox was surprised and angry. He shook his head and spat out the water.

The goose used his wings to push the bucket off. He ran to the pond and jumped in. He swam away from the fox. He was free and safe.

The ducks saw what happened. They stopped laughing and quacking. They felt sorry for the goose. They realized he was smart and brave. They swam to him and said sorry.

"Sorry, goose!" they said. "You are not silly. You are clever. You filled the bucket with water and used it to trick the fox. You saved yourself and us. You are our friend."

The goose felt happy and proud. He forgave the ducks. He said thank you.

"Thank you, ducks!" he said. "You are not mean. You are nice. You filled the pond with fun and friendship. You are my friends."

The goose and the ducks played and swam together. They shared the pond and the bucket. They filled their hearts with joy.

"Sure, you can lend my clay," Anna said. She gave Ben some of her clay. "But don't use all of it, okay? I still need some for my cat."

"Okay, I won't use all of it," Ben said. He took some of Anna's clay and started to make a dog. He made a head, a body, four legs, and a tail.

But then, he saw that Anna's cat had a very long tail. He thought that his dog should have a long tail too. So he took some more of Anna's clay and added it to his dog's tail. He made the tail longer and longer and longer.

"Hey, that's my clay!" Anna said, when she saw what Ben was doing. "You said you won't use all of it, but you did! Now I don't have enough clay for my cat!"

"I'm sorry, Anna," Ben said. "I just wanted to make a long tail for my dog. Here, you can have some of my clay. It's blue and green and yellow. It has a different texture. It's hard and rough and bumpy."

Anna looked at Ben's clay. She didn't like the colors or the texture. She wanted her own clay back. She felt sad and angry.

"No, thank you," she said. "I don't want your clay. I want my clay. You should give me back my clay. You are not a good friend. You are a bad friend."

Anna and Ben started to argue. They raised their voices and said mean words to each other. They forgot to have fun with the clay. They forgot to share and be kind.

Then, they heard a voice.

"Children, what's going on here?" It was their teacher, Mrs. Lee. She came to see what was wrong.

"Ben took all of my clay and made a long tail for his dog!" Anna said.

"Anna gave me her clay and then she wanted it back!" Ben said.

Mrs. Lee looked at the clay cat and the clay dog. She saw that they were both very nice, but they were also very different. She saw that Anna and Ben liked different things. She saw that they were both upset and hurt.

"Children, I understand that you both worked hard on your clay animals. They are very creative and beautiful. But I also see that you both made a mistake. You didn't respect each other's clay. You didn't listen to each other's wishes. You didn't say sorry or thank you. You didn't act like good friends. You acted like little children."

Anna and Ben felt ashamed. They knew that Mrs. Lee was right. They knew that they had been rude and selfish. They knew that they had hurt each other's feelings. They knew that they had to make up.

"Anna, I'm sorry for taking your clay. I should have asked you first. I should have given you some back. I should have been more careful. Can you forgive me?" Ben said.

"Ben, I'm sorry for yelling at you. I should have been more generous. I should have let you use some of my clay. I should have been more polite. Can you forgive me?" Anna said.

They looked at each other. They saw that they were both sorry. They saw that they were both friends.

"Yes, I forgive you," they said at the same time. They smiled and hugged.

"Good, I'm glad that you forgave each other," Mrs. Lee said. "Now, why don't you try to play with the clay together? Maybe you can learn from each other. Maybe you can mix the colors and the textures. Maybe you can make something new and fun."

Anna and Ben nodded. They agreed to play with the clay together. They decided to share and learn and have fun. They decided to be good friends. They decided to act like big children.

"No, these are my bananas! Go away!" the monkey said.

The monkey and the lion started to fight. They pulled and pushed and bit and scratched. They made a lot of noise.

Nearby, a wise old elephant was resting under a shady tree. He heard the noise and went to see what was happening. He saw the monkey and the lion fighting over the bananas.

"Stop fighting, you two!" the elephant said. "You are hurting each other and wasting your energy. Why don't you relax and share the bananas? There are enough for both of you. They are very tasty and good for you."

The monkey and the lion stopped fighting. They looked at the elephant. They looked at the bananas. They looked at each other. They felt ashamed.

"You are right, elephant. We are sorry. We were greedy and foolish. Thank you for your advice. We will relax and share the bananas." the monkey and the lion said.

They both apologized and made friends. They each took half of the bananas and ate them together. They enjoyed the bananas and each other's company. They thanked the elephant and said goodbye.

The elephant smiled and went back to his shady tree. He was glad that he helped the monkey and the lion. He relaxed and took a nap.

The moral of the story is: It is better to relax and share than to fight and be greedy.

"Wow, that is a very strange story, Lily," grandma says. "But I am glad you are safe and back with me. Maybe the fox was just lonely and wanted a friend. But you should not go into the woods alone. You never know what you might find."

Lily nods and agrees. She loves grandma and does not want to leave her. She thinks the fox is weird, but also a little sad. She wonders if the fox has any friends. But he was determined to play more, so he went back to the park and looked for something else fun to do. He found a small box and placed it on the floor. He took an object from inside the box and tried to shoot it into the air. The object spun and flew far away, but it made him happy. He kept shooting and playing until it was time to go home, tired but happy.

The sun was shining and the sky was bright blue. John and his mom were walking down the street when they heard a sound.

John said, "Mom, what was that noise?"

His mom said, "I think it's an elephant! Let's go and find it."

John and his mom walked around the corner and there was an elephant in the lake! The lake was very wet.

The elephant said, "Hi, John and Mom. Would you like to come and play?"

John and his mom said, "Sure!"

John and his mom played with the elephant in the wet lake until it was time to go home.

John said, "Bye, Elephant!"

The Elephant said, "Bye, John!"

Once there was a shy little girl named Jane. She was only three years old, but she was a very curious girl. One day, she went for a walk with her mom and dad. As they walked, Jane noticed a restaurant. She asked her mom and dad if they could go in and get something to eat.

They said yes, and the three of them went inside the restaurant. Jane was so happy, she smiled from ear to ear! But then she noticed something wasn't right. The restaurant was a little bit broken. There were some lights that weren't working, and the windows needed cleaning.

Jane's dad said, "Let's try to fix the restaurant". So they started to work. Jane and her mom cleaned the windows and her dad fixed the lights. When they were done, the restaurant looked so much better! Jane was so proud that she had helped to fix the restaurant. 

They had a wonderful meal, and afterwards, Jane said goodbye to the restaurant. Even though she was shy, she was happy that she had done her part to make it better.

Once upon a time there was a 3 year old little girl. She was always looking for ways to be creative and make things beautiful. One day she found an old rusty barrel in the front yard. Her eyes lit up! She immediately ran to her mom and asked, "Mommy, can I decorate it with beautiful colors and flowers?"

Her mom smiled, thinking of how creative and happy her daughter could be, and said, "Yes, you can decorate the barrel!"

The little girl excitedly ran outside with all her arts and crafts tools and got to work. She had lots of fun picking out soft colors and different textured flowers. 

When the little girl was finished with her masterpiece, she stepped back and beamed with pride. She showed her artwork to her mom, and she said, "Oh, my beautiful daughter, this piece is truly amazing! I'm so proud of your hard work and creativity. You have a special talent for making things even more beautiful."

The little girl hugged her mom and said, "Thank you for helping me discover my creativity. I can do anything I put my heart and mind to, even if it's something as small as decorating a barrel!"

This story has a moral value: With hard work and creativity, you can make something wonderful from even the simplest of things.

Once upon a time there was a stubborn boy named Jake. Jake liked to be in control all of the time, although his brother and sister didn't always let him.

One day Jake had a wild idea. He thought he could fly! He ran outside to the backyard, looked up at the sky and started running as fast as he could. But no matter how or how hard he tried, he just couldn't fly.

His brother and sister laughed and laughed. They thought it was silly that Jake thought he could fly. They just couldn't understand why Jake was so stubborn about it.

That night, Jake's mom made a salad for dinner. Jake thought about how he wished he could fly like a bird so he could take his plate of salad and eat it in the sky. He imagined how he could look down from up high and see all of his family eating together.

Jake knew he couldn't fly, but he was still stubborn about it. He never gave up on his dream of one day eating salad in the sky.

Once there was a bear who was very frustrated. He was upset because he couldn't solve a problem. He tried and tried, but he just couldn't figure it out.

Suddenly, he felt the cold air coming from a nearby cave. He decided to go to the cave to take a rest and clear his mind.

Inside the cave, he heard a beautiful sound. It was the sound of water trickling down the rocks into a little pool. The bear decided to stay and bathe in the pool.

He let all his worries out of his mind and felt calmer. He closed his eyes and sunk into the water.

It was the perfect moment. Suddenly, he heard a voice inside him saying "Release". So he did. He released his worries, his frustration, and all his bad feelings. He felt a million times better after that.

The bear learned that the best way to solve a problem was to take a break and release his worries.

As he was waiting, the old man heard a voice coming from the barrel. It was a magical voice! It said, "eat your soup and you will no longer be grumpy!"

Her mom smiled. "Sorry, honey," she said, "that is too high for you to reach."

Amelia frowned and thought for a moment. Then she said, "Maybe I can use a ladder to get to the top!"

Her mom laughed. "That's a great idea," she said.

The next day, Amelia got a ladder from the garage and carefully put it up next to the tall pole. Carefully, she climbed the ladder and reached the top. She carefully picked the flag and brought it down.

Amelia was very proud of herself. She had picked the flag from the very top of the tall pole.

Ben takes the diamond and looks at it closely. He sees how it sparkles in the light. He feels how it is smooth and hard. He tries to fit it with the other shapes, but it does not match.

"This shape is special," Ben says. "It does not belong with the other shapes. It is too beautiful and rare. We should keep it safe."

"Where should we keep it?" Lily asks.

Ben thinks for a moment. Then he has an idea.

"Let's dig a hole in the garden," he says. "We can bury the shape there. Then no one can take it away from us. It will be our secret treasure."

Lily likes the idea. She agrees with Ben. They take the diamond and a shovel and go to the garden. They find a spot under a big tree. They dig a deep hole and put the shape inside. They cover it with dirt and leaves. They pat the ground and smile at each other.

"We did it," Ben says. "We hid the shape. It is safe now. We can come back and see it anytime we want."

"Yes, we did," Lily says. "We are good friends. We share the shape. We love the shape."

They hug each other and go back to the house. They do not tell anyone about the shape. It is their secret. They love the shape. And they love each other.

Tom wants to get closer to the leopards. He thinks they are his friends. He climbs over the fence and jumps into the cage. He says hello to the leopards and tries to touch them. He does not know leopards are rare and wild and dangerous.

The leopards do not like Tom. They do not want him in their cage. They are angry and hungry. They attack Tom and bite him. Tom screams and cries. He is hurt and scared. He wishes he never imagined he was a leopard.

Mom and dad see Tom in the cage. They are shocked and scared. They call for help. The zoo workers come and try to save Tom. They use a big stick and a loud noise to make the leopards go away. They take Tom out of the cage and to the hospital.

Tom is very sorry. He learned a hard lesson. He will never imagine he is a leopard again. He will never go near a leopard again. He will never forget the day he met the leopards.

Tommy was very scared to go on the big slide at the park. He saw other kids slide down fast and scream with joy, but he thought it was too high and too steep. He hugged his blue teddy bear and stayed on the bench.

His big sister Anna saw him and came over. She smiled and said, "Tommy, do you want to try the slide? It's fun, I promise. I'll go with you and hold your hand."

Tommy shook his head and clutched his bear tighter. He said, "No, no, no. It's scary. I don't want to go."

Anna did not give up. She said, "Come on, Tommy. You can do it. You are brave and strong. Look, I have a belt for you. It will keep you safe and snug. You can wear it and I'll wear one too. Then we can slide together. It will be like flying."

She showed him a belt with a buckle and a strap. It was red and shiny. Tommy liked it. He looked at the slide again. It still looked scary, but he also felt curious. He wondered how it would feel to slide down. He said, "OK, maybe I'll try. But you have to hold my hand."

Anna nodded and said, "Of course I will. Come on, let's go." She helped him put on the belt and fastened it. Then she put on her own belt and took his hand. They walked to the slide and climbed the steps. Tommy felt his heart beat fast. He held his bear and his sister's hand.

They reached the top of the slide. Anna said, "Ready, Tommy? On the count of three, we'll slide. One, two, three!" She pushed them off and they slid down. Tommy felt the wind in his face and the slide under his body. He felt a thrill and a rush. He let go of his bear and raised his arms. He shouted, "Whee! This is fun!"

They reached the bottom and landed on the soft grass. Anna hugged him and said, "You did it, Tommy! You were amazing! How do you feel?"

Tommy smiled and said, "I feel good. I feel proud. I want to do it again!"

Anna said, "Me too! Let's go again!" They ran back to the slide, laughing and cheering. Tommy was not scared anymore. He was happy and brave. He thanked his sister for encouraging him. He said, "You are the best sister ever. I love you."

Anna said, "I love you too, Tommy. You are the best brother ever. Let's have fun!" They slid down again and again, until it was time to go home. They took off their belts and put them in their backpacks. They hugged their teddy bears and each other. They had a great day at the park.

Tim and Anna are friends. They like to play with trucks in the sand. Tim has a big red truck. Anna has a small blue truck. They make roads and bridges with the sand.

One day, Tim says to Anna, "I like your truck. Can I play with it?" Anna says, "Yes, you can. But you have to share your truck with me." Tim says, "OK, I will share. You are a good friend."

They play with their trucks for a long time. They have fun. Then, Tim says to Anna, "You are not only a good friend. You are also pretty. Do you want to marry me?" Anna says, "What is marry?" Tim says, "Marry is when you love someone and you stay with them forever. And you wear a ring and a dress and a suit. And you have a cake and a party."

Anna thinks for a moment. She says, "That sounds nice. But I don't have a ring or a dress or a suit. And I don't have a cake or a party." Tim says, "That's OK. We can use our trucks as rings. And we can wear our hats and coats. And we can have cookies and juice as cake and party."

Anna says, "OK, then. Let's marry." They put their trucks on their fingers. They put on their hats and coats. They find some cookies and juice. They say, "I love you" to each other. They hug and kiss. They are happy. They are married.

Ben and his mom went to the store to buy some food for dinner. Ben liked to sit in the front seat and pretend to drive the car. He held the wheel and made vroom-vroom noises.

"Mom, can I drive for real?" he asked.

"No, Ben, you are too little to drive. Driving is for grown-ups. You have to wait until you are big and strong," his mom said.

Ben was sad. He wanted to drive the car and go fast and honk the horn. He looked out the window and saw a huge truck. It was red and shiny and had a big trailer. Ben thought it was the coolest truck ever.

"Mom, look at that truck! It is huge! Can we drive that truck?" he asked.

"No, Ben, we can't drive that truck. That truck is for moving things. We have a car and it is just right for us. Besides, we have to go home and make dinner. What do you want to eat?" his mom said.

Ben thought for a moment. He liked pizza and chicken nuggets and macaroni and cheese. But he also liked something else.

"Mom, can we have ice cream for dinner?" he asked.

His mom laughed. "No, Ben, we can't have ice cream for dinner. Ice cream is for dessert. We have to eat something healthy first. How about some soup and salad and bread?" she said.

Ben made a face. He did not like soup and salad and bread. He wanted ice cream. He decided to try one more time.

"Mom, please, can we have ice cream for dinner? Just this once?" he asked.

His mom smiled. She knew Ben loved ice cream. She also knew he had been a good boy today. She decided to make a deal with him.

"OK, Ben, how about this. If you eat some soup and salad and bread, then you can have a small scoop of ice cream for dessert. But only if you eat your dinner first. Deal?" she said.

Ben nodded. He agreed to the deal. He was happy. He would eat his dinner and then he would have ice cream. He also hoped that one day he would be big enough to drive the car and the truck. He liked driving. Driving was fun.

Lily feels angry. She does not like the noise. She wants Max to be quiet. She says, "Max, stop! You are ruining our yoga!"

Max does not listen. He keeps playing with his cars. He says, "No, Lily, you stop! You are boring! Cars are better than yoga!"

Lily and Max start to argue. They yell and cry. They do not share or take turns. They do not listen to each other.

Their mom feels sad. She does not like to see them fight. She wants them to get along. She says, "Lily, Max, enough! You are both being rude and selfish. You need to close your mouths and open your ears. You need to respect each other and what you like to do. You need to apologize and say sorry."

Lily and Max stop yelling. They look at their mom. They see that she is serious and not happy. They feel sorry for making her sad. They feel sorry for being mean to each other.

They close their mouths and open their ears. They say, "Sorry, mom. Sorry, Lily. Sorry, Max."

They hug and make up. They decide to play together and take turns. They try to do yoga and cars. They find out that both are fun and make them feel good.

Their mom smiles and joins them. She is proud and happy. She says, "That's better. I love you both. You are my favorite bridge and car."

Ben did not stop. He pulled harder and harder. Anna felt scared and sad. She did not want to lose her doll. She looked around and saw a symbol on the wall. It was a cross. Her mom had told her that it was a symbol of love and hope. Anna remembered that and felt brave.

She said a little prayer in her heart and asked for help. She said, "Please, God, help me to resist Ben. He is not being fair. He is being greedy. Help me to be humble and kind. Help him to be humble and kind too. Amen."

Then, something happened. Ben suddenly let go of the doll. He looked at Anna and felt sorry. He realized that he was wrong. He said, "I'm sorry, Anna. I was bad. I should not have tried to take your doll. You can keep it. It is yours. Can we still be friends?"

Anna smiled and hugged her doll. She felt happy and relieved. She said, "It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. We can still be friends. Do you want to play with my doll and your car together?"

Ben nodded and smiled too. He said, "Yes, Anna. That sounds fun. Thank you for being nice to me."

They put their toys on the floor and played together. They shared and took turns. They were happy and humble. They did not fight anymore. They were good friends.

"What is this book?" Lily asks.

"I don't know. Maybe it is a story book," Tom says.

They open the book and see a page with a big star and a word. The word is "spell". Lily and Tom do not know what "spell" means.

"Spell? What is that?" Tom wonders.

"Maybe it is something magic," Lily guesses.

They look at the word and try to say it. They say "spell" together. Suddenly, something happens. The book glows and makes a sound. Lily and Tom are surprised and scared.

"What is happening?" Lily cries.

"I don't know. Let's close the book," Tom says.

They try to close the book, but it is too late. A bright light comes out of the book and takes them to another place. They see a castle, a dragon, a witch, and a knight. They are in a fairy tale.

"Wow! This is not our home. This is not modern. This is old and strange," Lily says.

"Maybe the book is a spell book. Maybe it can take us to different stories," Tom says.

"Maybe. But how do we go back?" Lily asks.

They look at the book, but it is closed and quiet. They do not know how to open it or how to say the word again. They are stuck in the fairy tale. They are in trouble.

Lily and Ben were playing doctor and patient in their room. Lily had a toy thermometer and a white coat. Ben had a blanket and a pillow.

"Open your mouth, Ben. I need to check your temperature," Lily said. She put the thermometer under Ben's tongue and waited. "Oh no, you have a fever. You are very hot."

Ben pretended to cough and sneeze. "I don't feel good, Lily. What can I do?"

Lily looked around the room. She saw some books, some toys, some crayons, and some clothes. The room was not organized. It was messy.

"You need to rest, Ben. And you need to clean your room. A messy room can make you sick. You have to include everything in the right place. Books go on the shelf, toys go in the box, crayons go in the drawer, and clothes go in the closet. Then your room will be organized and you will feel better."

Ben nodded. He did not like to clean, but he wanted to feel better. He got up from the bed and started to pick up his things. Lily helped him. They worked together until the room was organized.

"Good job, Ben. You are a good patient. And a good brother. Now you can lie down and rest. I will read you a story," Lily said. She took a book from the shelf and sat next to Ben. She opened the book and began to read. Ben smiled and closed his eyes. He felt better already.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to draw. They had many pencils of different colors, but their favorite was the red one. It was ancient, their mom said, and it belonged to their grandpa. He gave it to them before he went to the sky.

One day, they wanted to draw a big picture of their family. They took a big paper and the red pencil and started to draw. Ben drew mom and dad, and Lily drew grandpa and the dog. They were having fun, but they did not notice that the red pencil was getting shorter and shorter.

"Look, Ben, I'm almost done with grandpa's hat!" Lily said, holding up the paper.

"Me too, I just need to draw dad's glasses!" Ben said, looking at his paper.

They both reached for the red pencil, but it was too late. It broke in half, with a loud snap.

"Oh no!" they both cried. "The red pencil is broken! Now we can't finish our picture!"

They looked at each other, sad and angry. They both wanted the red pencil, and they both blamed each other for breaking it.

"It's your fault, Lily! You used it too much!" Ben said.

"No, it's your fault, Ben! You pressed it too hard!" Lily said.

They started to fight, pulling and pushing each other. They did not hear their mom calling them for lunch.

But they did not listen. They were too busy fighting over the red pencil.

They did not know that mom had a surprise for them. She had bought a new box of pencils, with many colors and shapes. She wanted to give it to them after lunch, as a reward for their drawing.

But they delayed their lunch, and their surprise, because of the red pencil. They did not realize that they had something more important than the red pencil: each other.

One day, a little bird was flying in the sky. He saw a big tree with many fruits. He wanted to eat some, but he was afraid of the other birds. They were bigger and louder than him.

He flew closer and saw a wise old owl sitting on a branch. The owl looked at him and said, "Hello, little bird. Do you want some fruits?"

The little bird nodded and said, "Yes, please. But the other birds are scary. They might hurt me."

The owl smiled and said, "Don't be afraid, little bird. You have a gift that they don't have. You can scatter the seeds of the fruits and make new trees grow. That is a good thing to do. The other birds only eat and waste the fruits. They don't care about the future."

The little bird was amazed and said, "Really? I can do that?"

The owl said, "Yes, you can. Just take a fruit and fly away. Then, find a distant place where there is no tree. Drop the seed on the ground and cover it with some dirt. Then, come back and do it again. Soon, you will see new trees growing and more fruits for everyone."

The little bird thanked the owl and did what he said. He took a fruit and flew away. He found a distant place where there was no tree. He dropped the seed on the ground and covered it with some dirt. Then, he came back and did it again.

The other birds saw him and laughed. They said, "Look at that silly bird. He is wasting the fruits. He is not smart like us. He is not strong like us. He is not brave like us."

But the little bird did not mind. He knew he was doing a good thing. He learned from the owl's wisdom. He was happy and proud.

The moral of the story is: Sometimes, the smallest and quietest ones can make the biggest and loudest difference.

One day, a boy named Ben and a girl named Lily wanted to sail on the lake. They found a big squash in the garden and thought it would make a good boat. They cut a hole in the squash and put a stick and a cloth for a sail. They pushed the squash into the water and climbed inside.

"Look, we are sailing!" Ben said. "This is fun!"

"Yes, it is!" Lily said. "But we should not go too far from the shore. The lake is big and deep."

But Ben did not listen. He wanted to sail faster and farther. He blew on the sail and made the squash go to the middle of the lake. Lily was scared. She saw the water was dark and the wind was strong.

"Ben, stop!" Lily said. "We have to go back. The squash is not a real boat. It might break or sink. We might get lost or wet."

But Ben did not listen. He thought Lily was silly and scared. He said, "Don't be crazy, Lily. The squash is a great boat. It is strong and fast. We can sail anywhere we want. We are having fun!"

But then, something bad happened. The wind blew harder and the water splashed harder. The squash started to crack and leak. The stick and the cloth fell off. The squash was not a boat anymore. It was just a squash.

"Help!" Ben and Lily cried. "We are in trouble!"

They were lucky. A man in a real boat saw them and came to help. He pulled them out of the water and took them to the shore. He was not happy. He said, "What were you thinking? You could have drowned. You should not sail on a squash. That is crazy. You should listen to your friend. She was right. You should be careful and safe."

Ben and Lily were sorry. They thanked the man and hugged each other. They learned a lesson. They learned that sailing on a squash was not fun. It was dangerous. They learned that they should not be crazy. They should be smart. They learned that they should listen to their friend. She was wise. They learned that they should be kind and respectful. They were friends.

They wrote about how they went to a cocoa factory and saw how cocoa was made. They were so happy with their story that they wanted to show it to their mom. They ran to the kitchen where their mom was making lunch. "Mom, mom, look at our story!" they said, holding their book. "We wrote about cocoa!"

Their mom smiled and took the book. She opened it and saw the pages full of colorful drawings and words. She read the story and praised Ben and Lily for their creativity and imagination. "What a wonderful story!" she said. "You are very good writers. How about we make some cocoa to celebrate?"

Ben and Lily cheered and hugged their mom. They helped her make some cocoa and poured it into their favorite mugs. They added some marshmallows and sprinkles and sat down at the table. He saw their book on the counter and grabbed it. He didn't care about their story. He only wanted to scribble on the pages with his own crayons. He made a big mess and ruined their story.

One day, Lily and Ben were playing hide and seek in the forest. Lily hid behind a tree and Ben looked for her. He sniffed the air and followed her smell. He found her and gave her a big hug.

"Ben, you are so hairy and dirty!" Lily said. "You need a wash!"

Ben did not like water. He was afraid of the river. He shook his head and growled.

"Please, Ben, let me wash you. You will feel better and smell nicer. I will be gentle and careful. I have a bucket and a sponge. Come with me!" Lily said.

She took Ben by the paw and led him to a small pond. She filled the bucket with water and wet the sponge. She rubbed the sponge on Ben's fur and made it clean and shiny. She sang a song to make him happy.

Ben felt the water and the sponge on his fur. He felt ticklish and curious. He saw his reflection in the pond and smiled. He looked handsome and bright. He liked the song and the wash.

"Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend. I like the wash. You are right. I feel better and smell nicer. Can we play some more?" Ben said.

Lily nodded and hugged him. They ran back to the forest and played until the sun went down. They were happy and clean.

Tom was a young boy who liked to play with his toys. He had a big box of cars, trains, and planes that he could make zoom and beep. He also had a soft toy monster that he called Rex. Rex was green and fuzzy, with horns, teeth, and a long tail. Tom loved Rex and hugged him every night.

One day, Tom was playing with his toys in his room, when he heard a loud clap from outside. He ran to the window and saw a big truck with a cage on the back. Inside the cage, there was a real monster! It was brown and scaly, with spikes, claws, and a short snout. It looked angry and scared, and it roared and banged on the bars.

Tom felt sorry for the monster. He wondered why it was in the cage and where it came from. He wanted to help it. He grabbed Rex and ran downstairs. He saw his mom in the kitchen and said, "Mom, mom, there's a monster outside! Can we go see it?"

His mom looked surprised and followed him to the door. She saw the truck and the monster and said, "Oh, Tom, that's not a monster. That's a dinosaur. It's a very old animal that lived a long time ago. The truck is taking it to the museum, where people can learn about it."

Tom was confused. He said, "But it looks like a monster. And it sounds like a monster. And it's in a cage like a monster. Why can't we go see it?"

His mom said, "Because it's not safe, Tom. The dinosaur is very big and strong, and it might hurt us if we get too close. And the truck is very fast and loud, and it might run us over if we cross the street. We have to stay here and watch from the window."

Tom felt sad. He said, "But I want to see the dinosaur. I want to be its friend. Maybe it's lonely and needs a hug. Like Rex."

His mom said, "I know, Tom, but you can't hug a dinosaur. It's not a toy. It's a wild animal. And it doesn't need a hug. It needs a home. The museum is its home, where it can be safe and happy. And you can see it there, when we go visit."

Tom thought about it. He said, "Okay, mom. I guess you're right. The dinosaur is not a monster. It's a dinosaur. And it's going to the museum. And we can see it there. But can I still clap for it? Maybe it will hear me and know that I like it."

His mom smiled and said, "Sure, Tom. You can clap for it. Maybe it will hear you and know that you're a nice boy."

Tom nodded and said, "Okay, mom. Thank you." He held Rex in one arm and clapped with the other. He watched the truck and the dinosaur drive away. He hoped the dinosaur would be safe and happy. He hoped it would find a friend. Like Rex.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried. He held his hand. It was red and swollen. A bee had stung him.

"Ben got stung by a bee," Anna said. "He wanted honey, but he did not listen to me. He touched the bee's flower."

Mom looked at Ben and said, "Oh, poor Ben. You should be more careful. Bees are good, but they need their flowers. They work hard to make honey. You should not take their flowers. You should say sorry to the bees."

Ben nodded. He was still in pain, but he felt bad for the bees. He put the ice on his hand and said, "I'm sorry, bees. I will not touch your flowers again. Thank you for making honey."

Ben smiled too and said, "Yes, Anna. That sounds nice. I love honey. And I love you."

They hugged and went inside to have some juice and cookies. They were happy and learned a lesson.

But then, the sky gets dark and the wind blows hard. The snow starts to fall again. It is very cold.

Lily and Tom were having breakfast with Mom and Dad. They liked to eat cereal with milk and fruit. Lily had a pink spoon and Tom had a blue spoon. They were happy and hungry.

But then Tom saw something on the table. It was a shiny sticker with a star. He wanted the sticker for his book. He reached out and grabbed it. But it was stuck to a paper. He tried to pull it off, but he could not.

"Hey, that's mine!" Lily said. She saw Tom with her sticker. She was angry and sad. She loved her sticker. She had got it from her teacher for being good. She wanted it back.

"No, it's mine!" Tom said. He did not want to give it back. He liked the sticker too. He thought it was great. He wanted it for himself.

They both pulled the paper with the sticker. They pulled hard. They pulled harder. They pulled too hard. The paper tore in half. The sticker tore too. It was ruined.

They both cried. They both felt bad. They had broken the sticker and the paper. They had hurt each other's feelings.

Mom and Dad heard the noise. They came to the table. They saw the mess. They saw the tears. They were not happy.

"What happened here?" Mom asked. She looked at Lily and Tom. She wanted to know the truth.

"We were fighting over the sticker," Lily said. She sniffed. She was sorry.

"We tore it by mistake," Tom said. He sobbed. He was sorry too.

Mom and Dad sighed. They hugged Lily and Tom. They understood. They knew they both liked the sticker. They knew they both made a mistake.

"It's okay," Mom said. She wiped their tears. She smiled. "We can fix this. We can glue the paper and the sticker back together. We can share it. We can put it on the fridge. We can all enjoy it."

"Really?" Lily asked. She brightened. She liked that idea.

"Really," Tom said. He nodded. He liked that idea too.

They both said sorry to each other. They both said thank you to Mom and Dad. They both finished their breakfast. They both used their spoons. They were happy again. They had learned a lesson. They had learned to be kind and fair. They had learned to share.

Suddenly, her friend Tom leaned over. He reached into her lap and clicked the buckle together. When it was done, he said, "That's it! Now you're safe."

Kate smiled at him. But then the bus driver shouted again. This time he said, "Everyone must check their seat belts. I'm demanding that you do it now!" Everyone knew it was very important, so they all checked their buckles.

After that, the bus journey was calm and peaceful. Everyone rode safely and the driver was very happy. He smiled as the children looked out of the window, enjoying the hot sunshine.

Her dad laughed and said, "Rachel, that's not a squash! That's a lemon!" Rachel felt her face drop. She didn't want a sour lemon, she wanted a yummy squash! She put down the lemon and looked down sadly. 

But then her dad picked up the lemon, smiled and said, "You can still use it! We can make some delicious lemonade!" Rachel's eyes lit up and her face turned into a big grin. They went inside and made the most delicious and sour lemonade Rachel had ever tasted!

At the veterinarian, the nice doctor looked at Spot's tooth. The doctor said, "Spot, you need to be careful when you bite hard things." The veterinarian fixed Spot's tooth, and he felt so much better. Spot and his mom went home, and he promised to be more careful when biting things.

One day, a little fish named Fin went to the big lake for a swim. He saw a great big fish, who was very strong. Fin wanted to be friends with the big fish, so he swam up to him and said, "Hello! Do you want to play with me?"

The big fish looked at Fin and said, "I'm too big to play with you. You are too small." Fin was sad, but he wanted to show the big fish that he could be strong too.

Fin saw a heavy rock and thought, "If I move this rock, the big fish will see how strong I am!" Fin tried to push the rock. He started to struggle. He pushed and pushed, but the rock did not move.

The big fish saw Fin struggle and laughed. He said, "I told you, you are too small." Then, the big fish swam away, leaving Fin all alone. Fin was very sad, and he never saw the big fish again.

"Hello, little fox. What are you doing here?" the owl asked.

"I was just exploring the forest. I saw your hole and wanted to see what was inside. What are you doing here?" the little fox answered.

"I am caring for my eggs. They are the last ones I have. I have no mate and no friends. I am alone and lonely," the owl said.

The owl was surprised and touched by the little fox's words. He said, "You want to be my friend? But you are a fox and I am an owl. We are different. How can we be friends?"

The little fox and the owl became friends. They visited each other every day. They watched over the eggs until they hatched. They taught the baby owls how to fly and hunt. They had fun and joy in the forest.

The moral of the story is: Caring for others can make you happy and bring you friendship.

Ant says, "OK, I will wait and be quiet. Thank you, Bee. You are a good friend."

Bee flies to the hive and takes some honey. He comes back and gives it to Ant. Ant tastes the honey and smiles. He says, "This is the best honey ever. Thank you, Bee. You are a brave friend."

Bee and Ant share the honey and enjoy it. They are happy and grateful. They discuss how to find more flowers and make more honey. They are good friends.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play together. They had a big box that they pretended was a house. They cut out windows and doors with scissors and drew pictures on the walls. They said they were married and happy.

One day, Lily found a shiny ring in her mom's drawer. She thought it was pretty and put it on her finger. She showed it to Tom and said, "Look, this is my wedding ring. It means I love you forever." Tom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily. You are the best wife ever."

But then, Lily's mom came and saw the ring. She was angry and said, "Lily, that is not your ring. That is my ring. Your dad gave it to me when we got married. But he left us and broke our marriage. He broke my heart. Give me back my ring now!"

Lily was scared and sad. She did not want to give back the ring. She did not want to lose Tom. She said, "No, mom, this is my ring. Tom and I are married. We are happy. We will not break our marriage. We will not break our hearts."

Lily's mom was very sad and cried. She said, "Lily, you don't understand. Marriage is not a game. It is a promise. Sometimes, people break their promises and hurt each other. Sometimes, things get broken and can't be fixed. You are too young to know what marriage means. You are too young to wear this ring. Please, give it back to me. It is the only thing I have left from your dad."

Lily looked at Tom and saw that he was also sad. He said, "Lily, I love you, but I think your mom is right. We are not really married. We are just playing. The ring is not ours. It belongs to your mom. She needs it more than we do. Let's give it back to her and say sorry. Maybe we can find another way to show our love."

Lily thought for a moment and realized that Tom was right. She took off the ring and gave it to her mom. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I didn't mean to hurt you. I love you. I love Tom too. But we are not married. We are just friends. Can we still play together?"

Lily's mom hugged her and said, "Of course, you can, my sweet girl. I love you too. And I'm proud of you for being honest and kind. You are a good friend to Tom. And maybe, one day, when you grow up, you will find someone who will love you and keep his promises. Someone who will not break your marriage. Someone who will not break your heart."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of honesty, kindness, and respect for other people's feelings and belongings. It also shows the difference between playing and reality, and the meaning and challenges of marriage.

Foreshadowing or setup and payoff: The story uses foreshadowing when Lily finds the ring in her mom's drawer, which hints at the conflict that will arise later. It also uses setup and payoff when Lily and Tom cut out windows and doors for their box house, which contrasts with the broken marriage and heart of Lily's mom.

"No, I like the laser. It is fun and cool. You are grumpy, Sara. You do not like anything," Ben said. He kept making the laser go pew pew and shine it on the wall.

Sara got very angry. She wanted Ben to stop. She grabbed her doll and threw it at Ben. But she missed. The doll hit the lamp and the lamp fell over. The lamp made a loud crash and broke.

Mom heard the noise and came to the living room. She saw the broken lamp and the doll and the laser. She was not happy.

"What happened here?" Mom asked. "Who broke the lamp?"

Sara and Ben looked at each other. They did not want to get in trouble. They did not say anything.

Mom looked at them. She knew they were both guilty. She said, "You two need to learn to share and play nicely. No more laser or doll for today. You have to clean up this mess and go to your rooms."

Sara and Ben felt sorry. They wished they had not fought. They wished they had not broken the lamp. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We will not do it again."

They picked up the pieces of the lamp and the doll and the laser. They put them in a box. They went to their rooms. They did not kick or scream. They learned their lesson.

Lily crouched down and saw the cutest, furry black kitten curled up in the corner.

"Hi there, little one!" she whispered excitedly.

Suddenly the kitten hissed and Lily jumped back.

"Whoa!" she exclaimed.

Lily was about to forget all about the rude, unfriendly kitten when she noticed something disgusting on the floor.

When she moved closer she realised it was scrambled egg! The kitten had obviously found the eggs that Lily had forgotten to put away in the kitchen. She sighed, feeling guilty - she had been so excited about getting the kitten she had totally forgotten to put the eggs away.

But the kitten meowed softly and the guilt disappeared. Lily reached out to pat her new friend, who purred happily at her touch. 

"Looks like we're going to be friends after all," Lily smiled.

The man called a carpenter to see if he could help stop the hangers from shaking. But no matter what the carpenter did, the hangers kept shaking!

The rich man didn't know what to do, and he was very sad. Then he heard a loud noise coming from inside his wall. He finally realized that it was an earthquake shaking the hangers!

The earthquake was so powerful that it destroyed the rich man's house and all his hangers. Sadly, the rich man lost everything he owned. He had to start from scratch.

But it was not true; Floyd was lying. 

The next day Floyd and Olive were playing in the fields again and saw the same turtle. But this time, Olive was very unhappy as she knew Floyd had lied to her and the turtle was not his. She refused to play and became upset. 

Floyd felt very sad, so he went to Olive and apologised. He explained that he just wanted to make her happy, but he should not have lied to her. Olive understood that he was sorry and was happy again. 

So, the moral of this story is that it is never ok to lie to someone you care about, even if it's to make them happy. It is better to be honest and tell the truth.

On a warm summer day, a bunny named Bob hopped through the tall grass. He had been running for a long time and he was tired. Bob was looking for a place to rest. Just then, he heard something behind him and he started to tremble.

Bob was scared, but he slowly turned around. He saw a cat, who was much bigger than him. The cat had large muscles and looked very strong. Bob was scared, but he was also brave. He had to do something.

Bob took a deep breath and stepped forward. He tried not to tremble. Then, he made a cool move. He said, "I'll give you something if you don't hurt me."

The cat thought for a moment and then, he said, "Okay, I won't hurt you." To Bob's surprise, the cat helped him find a place to hide.

The moral of the story is simple: be brave and kind. Even if you're scared, it's important to try and do the right thing. You never know what could happen.

The frog croaked, "I need to wear them. I want to look awesome like you!"

One day, his mom gave him a prune for a snack. Timmy hated prunes. He wanted a cookie or a candy. He spat out the prune and yelled at his mom. He said he hated her and ran to his room. He slammed the door and cried.

His mom was very sad and angry. She decided to teach him a lesson. She took away all his toys and snacks from his room. She left only a prune on his bed. She locked the door and said he could not come out until he ate the prune and said sorry.

Timmy was very scared and lonely. He looked for his toys and snacks, but he could not find them. He saw the prune on his bed, but he did not want to eat it. He banged on the door and screamed, but his mom did not answer. He felt hungry and thirsty. He wished he had been nice to his mom and his sister and his friends.

He realized he had been a bad boy. He decided to eat the prune and say sorry. He crawled to his bed and picked up the prune. He took a bite and swallowed. It was not so bad. He took another bite and finished it. He felt better. He said, "Mom, I'm sorry. I love you. Please let me out."

His mom heard him and came to his door. She unlocked it and opened it. She saw him sitting on his bed with a smile. She hugged him and said, "I love you too, Timmy. I'm glad you ate the prune and said sorry. You learned your lesson. Next time, be more grateful and kind."

Timmy followed his mom and said, "Okay, mom. I'm sorry, sister. I'm sorry, friends. Can I share with you?"

They all said, "Yes, Timmy. We forgive you. Let's play together."

Timmy was happy. He learned to be more humble and generous. He never threw tantrums or spat out prunes again. He became a good boy.

Ben is a painter. He likes to make pictures with colors. He has a big brush and a small brush. He has red, blue, yellow, green, and white colors. He paints on a big paper on the wall.

Sam is Ben's brother. He is three years old. He likes to play with toys. He has a car, a ball, a bear, and a dinosaur. He plays on the floor.

One day, Ben is painting a picture of a flower. He uses red, yellow, and green colors. He is happy with his picture. He says, "Look, Sam, I made a flower. Do you like it?"

Sam looks at the picture. He does not like it. He thinks it is boring. He says, "No, I don't like it. It is not fun. It is not a toy. I want to play with your brushes and colors."

Ben says, "No, Sam, you can't play with my brushes and colors. They are mine. They are for painting. You have your toys. Go play with them."

Sam gets angry. He wants to play with the brushes and colors. He thinks they are more fun than his toys. He says, "No, I want to play with them. Give them to me. Now!"

Ben says, "No, Sam, go away. Leave me alone. I am painting."

Sam does not go away. He tries to grab the brushes and colors from Ben. Ben tries to stop him. They fight. They push and pull. They yell and cry.

Mom hears them. She comes to see what is wrong. She sees them fighting. She sees the paper on the wall. She sees the colors on the floor. She is not happy. She says, "Stop, Ben and Sam. Stop fighting. What are you doing? Look at this mess. You are making a big problem."

Ben and Sam stop fighting. They look at Mom. They look at the paper. They look at the colors. They see they made a big problem. They feel bad. They say, "Sorry, Mom. Sorry, Ben. Sorry, Sam."

They both grabbed the star scissors and tried to take them from each other. They pulled and pushed and tugged. The scissors slipped and cut Lily's finger. She cried out in pain and dropped the scissors. Ben saw the blood and felt sorry. He dropped the scissors too and hugged Lily.

"I'm sorry, Lily. Are you okay?" Ben asked.

Lily sobbed and showed him her finger. It was bleeding a lot. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was mean. It hurts."

Ben said, "Let's go to mom. She can help you. And we can say sorry to her too. We broke the rule and the scissors."

They ran to the door and opened it. They saw mom standing there with a worried face. She had heard the noise and came back. She saw the blood, the scissors, and the paper. She said, "Oh, no. What happened? Are you okay?"

Lily and Ben told her what happened. They said sorry and hugged her. Mom said, "It's okay. I'm glad you're sorry. But you have to be careful with scissors. They are not toys. They can hurt you and others. And you have to share and take turns. That's the rule."

She took Lily to the bathroom and cleaned her finger. She put a band-aid on it and kissed it. She said, "There. It will be better soon. But you have to be more careful next time."

Lily nodded and smiled. She said, "Thank you, mom. I love you."

Mom said, "I love you too. And you, Ben. Come here and give me a hug."

Ben hugged mom and said, "I love you, mom. And I love you, Lily. I'm sorry I fought with you."

Lily said, "I love you too, Ben. And I'm sorry I fought with you."

Mom said, "That's good. Now, let's go and clean up the mess. And then we can have some cookies and milk. How does that sound?"

Lily and Ben said, "That sounds great!"

They went to their room and picked up the paper and the scissors. They put them away and said goodbye to the star scissors. They said, "Maybe we can use you again someday. But only if we are careful and nice."

They followed mom to the kitchen and had some cookies and milk. They talked and laughed and forgot about the fight. They were happy and learned a lesson. They decided to share and take turns and be careful with scissors. And they never mentioned the star scissors again.

One day, a boy named Ben saw a squirrel in his yard. He liked the squirrel and wanted to play with it. He ran to the squirrel and said, "Hi, squirrel! Do you want to be my friend? I can invite you to my house and we can have fun!"

The stick hit the squirrel and the squirrel fell down. Ben ran to the squirrel and saw that it was not moving. He touched the squirrel and felt that it was cold and stiff. He realized that the squirrel was dead.

Ben started to cry. He felt sorry for the squirrel and for what he had done. He wished he could make the squirrel alive again. He heard his mom calling him from the house. He left the squirrel and ran to his mom. He told her what happened and how he felt. His mom hugged him and said, "Ben, I'm sorry for your loss. But you should not have thrown the stick at the squirrel. That was very mean and dangerous. You could have hurt the squirrel or yourself. You should always be gentle and respectful to animals. They are living things, just like us. They have feelings and needs. They are not toys or enemies. They are part of nature and we should care for them."

Ben nodded and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I understand. I will never do that again. I will be nice to animals and try to make friends with them. Maybe I can find another squirrel and invite it to play with me. But I will not chase it or throw things at it. I will let it come to me if it wants to."

His mom smiled and said, "That's a good idea, Ben. I'm proud of you for learning from your mistake. Now, let's go and bury the squirrel and say a prayer for it. Maybe it will forgive you and be happy in heaven."

Ben and his mom went to the yard and dug a hole for the squirrel. They put the squirrel in the hole and covered it with dirt. They said a prayer and thanked the squirrel for being part of their world. They put some flowers and nuts on the grave and said goodbye. If they touch you, you have to freeze and not move until someone else touches you. Tommy is very fast and good at freeze tag. He is popular and everyone wants to be on his team.

One day, Tommy sees a new kid at the park. His name is Ben and he has a big bag of broccoli. Tommy thinks broccoli is yucky and green. He does not want to play with Ben. He tells his friends to ignore Ben and play freeze tag without him. Ben looks sad and lonely. He sits on a bench and eats his broccoli.

Tommy is it and runs after his friends. He touches Lily and she freezes. He touches Sam and he freezes. He touches Mia and she freezes. Soon, all his friends are frozen and Tommy is the only one who can move. He feels happy and proud. He is the best at freeze tag.

But then, he hears a voice behind him. "Tag, you're it!" It is Ben. He has sneaked up on Tommy and touched him with his broccoli. Tommy feels a cold and wet broccoli on his back. He is shocked and disgusted. He has to freeze and not move. He does not like this at all.

Ben runs to Tommy's friends and touches them. They unfreeze and smile. They thank Ben and say he is nice and brave. They ask him to join their game and be on their team. Ben is happy and shares his broccoli with them. They say broccoli is yummy and healthy. They become friends and play freeze tag together.

Tommy is still frozen and alone. He feels sad and sorry. He wishes he had been nicer to Ben and tried his broccoli. He learns a lesson. He should not judge people by what they eat or how they look. He should be kind and friendly to everyone. He hopes Ben and his friends will forgive him and let him play with them again. He waits for someone to touch him and unfreeze him. He hopes it is not another broccoli.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the woods. They had a big stick that they called a spear. They used it to pretend they were hunters and chase rabbits and squirrels. One day, they saw a big red berry bush. They ran to it and picked some berries to eat.

"Yum, these are sweet and juicy!" Tom said.

"Let me try!" Sam said. He took a berry from Tom's hand and put it in his mouth. But he made a face and spat it out. "Blech, this is sour!"

Tom laughed. "You picked a bad one. Here, have another one." He gave Sam a different berry.

Sam looked at it and saw it was smaller and darker than the one he had before. He remembered that his mom had told him not to eat berries that looked like that. They could make him sick. He shook his head and pushed Tom's hand away.

"No, thank you. I don't want any more berries. Let's go play with the spear."

Tom frowned. He thought Sam was being silly and rude. He wanted to share his berries with him. He decided to play a trick on him. He took the sour berry that Sam had spat out and hid it behind his back. He followed Sam to the spear and pretended to be friendly.

"Hey, Sam, let's see who can throw the spear farther. You go first."

Sam smiled. He liked to play with the spear. He picked it up and threw it as hard as he could. It flew through the air and landed on a tree.

"Wow, that was far! Good job, Sam!" Tom said. He clapped his hands. Then he quickly ran to the spear and grabbed it. He also took the sour berry from behind his back and stuck it on the tip of the spear. He hoped Sam would not notice.

"Thanks, Tom. Now it's your turn. Let's see if you can beat me." Sam said.

Tom nodded. He held the spear in his hand and aimed at the tree. He threw it with all his might. But he threw it too high. The spear went over the tree and disappeared in the bushes.

"Oh, no! Where did it go?" Tom said. He ran to the bushes and looked for the spear. He could not find it.

Sam followed him and helped him look. He saw something shiny in the grass. He picked it up and saw it was the sour berry. He recognized it from before. He realized what Tom had done. He was angry.

"Tom, you tried to trick me! You put this sour berry on the spear. That was mean!" Sam said.

Tom felt ashamed. He knew he had done something wrong. He wished he had not done it. He wanted to say sorry, but he could not find the words.

"Sam, I..." he started to say.

But Sam did not want to hear him. He threw the sour berry at Tom's face and ran away. He did not want to play with him anymore.

Tom felt sad. He had lost his spear and his brother. He wished he could take it back. He learned a hard lesson. He should not play tricks on people he loved. He should be kind and share. He hoped Sam would forgive him someday. He hoped he would find his spear too. He did not like the taste of sour berries.

"Ben, what did you do?" Lily shouted. "You made a big mess!"

"I don't like your soup!" Ben said. "It's gross!"

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play and learn together. One day, Lily wants to teach Tom how to make a picnic. She says, "A picnic is when you eat outside on a blanket. You need food, drinks, plates and napkins. I will show you how to make a picnic."

They go to the kitchen and find some bread, cheese, jam, apples and juice. Lily helps Tom cut the bread and cheese. She spreads jam on some bread. She puts the food in a basket. She also takes some plates and napkins. She says, "Now we have a picnic. Let's go outside and find a nice spot."

They go to the park and look for a shady place under a tree. The sun is bright and warm. They spread a blanket on the grass and put the basket on it. They sit down and start to eat. They share the bread, cheese, jam, apples and juice. They say, "Mmm, this is yummy. We like picnics."

They finish their food and drink. They wipe their mouths and hands with the napkins. They pack everything back in the basket. They say, "Thank you for the picnic, Lily. You are a good teacher, Tom. We had fun."

They fold the blanket and carry the basket. They walk back to the house, holding hands. They smile and laugh. They are happy. They are friends.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big monkey on a tree. The monkey had a long tail and a big mouth. The monkey was holding a banana.

"Look, a monkey!" Lily said. "Can we give him a hug?"

"No, he is ugly and scary!" Tom said. "He might bite us!"

The monkey heard them and got angry. He threw the banana at them. The banana hit Tom on the head. Tom started to cry.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom said. "The banana hurts!"

Lily ran to Tom and hugged him. She saw the monkey making a loud noise. The monkey was showing his teeth and shaking his fist.

"Shh, shh, shh!" Lily said. "Don't cry, Tom. The monkey is just mean. He is not nice like us."

The monkey saw that Lily and Tom were not afraid of him. He felt lonely and sad. He wished he had a friend to play with. He climbed down from the tree and walked to Lily and Tom. He gave them a small smile and a soft grunt.

"Hello, monkey," Lily said. "Do you want to be our friend?"

The monkey nodded and offered them his banana. Lily and Tom smiled and took the banana. They broke it in half and shared it with the monkey. The monkey was happy and wagged his tail.

"Thank you, monkey," Tom said. "You are not ugly and scary. You are nice and funny."

The monkey, Lily and Tom became friends. They played in the park until it was time to go home. They said goodbye and hugged each other. The monkey waved and climbed back to his tree. He was not lonely and sad anymore. He was glad he met Lily and Tom.

One day, a big boy comes to the park. He sees the orange ball. He wants the ball. He runs to the ball and grabs it. He says, "This is my ball now. Go away!"

Tom and Mia are sad and angry. They want their ball back. They say, "No, this is our ball. Give it back!" But the big boy does not listen. He laughs and runs away with the ball.

The big boy is shocked. He says, "Hey, what are you doing? Give me the ball!" He tries to open the zip. But the zip is locked. He can't open it. He says, "No, no, no! This is not fair!"

Tom and Mia smile. They say, "Yes, yes, yes! This is fair! This is our ball. You can't have it. You are mean!" They run away from the big boy. They go to another park. They play with their orange ball. They are happy.

The nurse came with a bag of tools. She had a thermometer, a stethoscope, a flashlight and a band-aid. She smiled at Lily and said hello. She asked Lily to open her mouth and put the thermometer under her tongue. Lily did not like it. She spit it out and cried. She did not want the nurse to touch her.

The nurse was patient. She said she was sorry and tried to calm Lily down. She explained that she needed to see how hot Lily was and listen to her heart and lungs. She said it would not hurt and it would be very quick. She asked Lily's mom to help her. Lily's mom hugged Lily and said it was okay. She said the nurse was here to help her feel better. She said she would allow the nurse to do her job if Lily was brave and cooperated.

Lily was scared but she trusted her mom. She nodded and let the nurse put the thermometer back in her mouth. She held still and waited for the beep. The nurse looked at the number and said it was high. She said Lily had a serious infection and needed some medicine. She used the stethoscope to listen to Lily's chest and back. She used the flashlight to look at Lily's ears and throat. She said Lily had an earache and a tonsillitis. She put a band-aid on Lily's arm where she gave her a shot. She said the shot would help Lily fight the germs.

Lily was brave and did not cry anymore. She said thank you to the nurse and gave her a hug. The nurse said she was proud of Lily and gave her a sticker. She said Lily had to rest and drink a lot of water. She said she would come back tomorrow to see how Lily was doing. She said goodbye and left with her bag of tools. Lily's mom kissed Lily and said she loved her. She said she would make her some soup and read her a story. Lily smiled and cuddled with her teddy bear. She felt a little better. She hoped the nurse would bring her another sticker tomorrow.

"I imagine that I have a big family. They are very nice and reliable. They always love me and take care of me. Do you like my imaginary family, mom?" she said.

Her mom smiled and hugged her. "I like your imaginary family, Lily. They sound wonderful. But you know what? You already have a real family that is very nice and reliable. They always love you and take care of you. Do you know who they are?" she said.

Dan is a bald man. He has no hair on his head. He likes to wear hats to keep his head warm. One day, he goes to the park with his dog, Rex. Rex is a big, brown dog. He likes to run and play.

At the park, Dan sees a big tree. The tree has many green leaves. The leaves spread wide and make a lot of shade. Dan thinks the tree is nice. He takes off his hat and sits under the tree. He feels the cool breeze on his bald head.

Rex sees a squirrel. The squirrel is small and gray. It has a long, fluffy tail. Rex wants to chase the squirrel. He barks and runs after it. The squirrel is scared. It runs up the tree. Rex jumps and tries to catch it, but he is too slow.

The squirrel reaches the top of the tree. It looks down and sees Rex. It sees Dan too. It sees Dan's bald head. It thinks Dan's head is a big, shiny nut. It wants to eat the nut. It jumps from the tree and lands on Dan's head.

Dan feels something on his head. He looks up and sees the squirrel. He is surprised and scared. He screams and shakes his head. The squirrel is surprised and scared too. It screams and jumps off Dan's head. It runs away.

Rex hears Dan and the squirrel. He runs back to Dan. He sees the squirrel running away. He barks and chases it again. Dan puts on his hat and laughs. He thinks Rex and the squirrel are funny. He is happy. He pets Rex and says, "Good boy, Rex. Good boy."

One day, she saw a poster on the wall. It said: "Do you like music? Come and join our band! We need a drummer, a flutist, and a guitarist. We will play at the park on Saturday. Everyone is welcome!"

Sara was happy. She wanted to join the band. She took her drum, her flute, and her guitar, and went to the park. She saw some kids playing music. They had a piano, a violin, and a trumpet. They saw Sara and smiled.

"Hi, we are the band. What is your name?" they asked.

"I am Sara. I like music. Can I play with you?" Sara said.

"Of course, you can. We need a drummer, a flutist, and a guitarist. You have all of them. Come and join us!" they said.

Sara was very happy. She played her drum, her flute, and her guitar with the band. They made beautiful music together. They had fun. They became friends.

Sara was not lonely anymore. She learned that music can bring people together. She learned that she can make friends by sharing her talents. She learned that she is not alone.

Sara did not like Ben pulling her. She wanted the magazine. She pulled back and said, "Let go, Ben, let go! I want the magazine!"

Sara and Ben knew they were in trouble. They wished they had listened to Mom. They wished they had stayed in their chairs. They wished they had not touched the magazines. They leaned together and hoped Mom would not be too angry.

Lila shrugged. She did not care what Ben wanted. She liked her blocks and did not want to give any away.

Ben was sad. He tried to make a tower with his blocks, but it was too small and weak. It fell down easily. He looked at Lila's tower. It was big and strong. It did not fall down.

Ben had an idea. He saw a ball on the floor. It was big and round and flexible. He picked it up and threw it at Lila's tower. The ball hit the tower and made it fall down. The blocks crashed and scattered.

Lila was angry. She screamed and cried. She ran to Ben and pushed him. Ben fell down and dropped the ball.

"Why did you do that? You broke my tower!" Lila yelled.

"I wanted some of your blocks, but you did not share. You were mean to me," Ben said.

Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lila and Ben fighting and the blocks all over the floor. She was not happy.

"What are you doing? Why are you fighting? Why did you make such a mess?" Mom asked.

Lila and Ben stopped fighting. They looked at Mom. They felt bad. They did not know what to say.

Mom picked up the ball and held it in her hand. She felt its weight. She squeezed it and saw how flexible it was.

"Do you know what this is?" Mom asked.

"A ball," Lila and Ben said.

"Yes, a ball. A ball is for playing, not for throwing. A ball is for sharing, not for keeping. A ball is for having fun, not for making trouble. Do you understand?" Mom asked.

Lila and Ben nodded. They understood.

Mom gave the ball to Lila and Ben. She told them to share it and play nicely. She told them to pick up the blocks and put them away. She told them to say sorry to each other and hug.

Lila and Ben did what Mom said. They shared the ball and played nicely. They picked up the blocks and put them away. They said sorry to each other and hugged.

They felt better. They smiled and laughed. They were friends again.

Lila was a gifted girl who loved to play the violin. She could make beautiful sounds with her violin and everyone liked to hear her. She played the violin every day and night, even when it was time to sleep.

But Lila did not like to sleep. She thought sleep was boring and a waste of time. She wanted to play the violin more and more, and she did not listen to her mom and dad who told her to sleep. They said sleep was good for her health and her mind, and that she would play better if she slept well.

One night, Lila played the violin so late that she fell asleep with it in her arms. She did not hear the fire alarm that went off in her house. She did not smell the smoke that filled her room. She did not feel the heat that burned her skin. She did not wake up when the firemen came to save her. She slept and slept and never woke up again.

Tina thought for a moment. She was still angry, but she stepped closer to Tom and he hugged her and then whispered something.

"The empty feeling we get after a fight is not worth it," he said.

Tina suddenly understood and she hugged Tom back. She whispered in his ear, "Let's not fight anymore, let's be friends."

Tom nodded and smiled at her. They went back to playing and this time, they were happier than before.

The moral of the story is that it's not worth it to fight, because eventually, you will still be left with an empty feeling inside. We can resolve our disagreements by talking calmly and understanding each other.

The little girl picked up the folder and showed it to Mittens. Mittens saw the picture and realized that he was missing out on fun. He decided to wake up and play with the little girl. They played together all day and Mittens had a lot of fun. From that day on, Mittens wasn't lazy anymore and loved to play with his new friend.

Once upon a time, a boy named Timmy went to play outside on his street. He saw a slide and wanted to play on it. But, another boy was already on the slide and didn't let Timmy play.

Timmy asked, "Can I please slide too?"

The other boy said, "No, go away!"

Timmy got angry and said, "That's not nice! I want to play too!"

The other boy realized he was being mean and said, "Okay, you can slide too. Sorry for being mean."

Timmy smiled and they both slid down the slide together. They became friends and played together all day on the street. The end.
