Mom and Dad nod. They pack up their things and take Lily and Tom to another part of the beach. There, the water is clean and clear and not smelly. Lily and Tom are happy. They splash and swim and have fun. They forget about the sign and the fish and enjoy the ocean.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play football in the park. They have a beautiful football. It is red and white and shiny.

One day, they see a big tree in the park. The tree has many branches and leaves. Tom has an idea. He says to Sam, "Let's attach our football to the tree. It will look like a big apple. It will be fun."

Sam thinks it is a good idea. He helps Tom to attach the football to the tree. They use a rope and a stick. They are happy. They laugh and clap.

But then, a bird comes. The bird sees the football. The bird thinks it is a big apple. The bird is hungry. It pecks the football. It makes a hole. The air comes out. The football becomes flat.

Tom and Sam are sad. They cry and shout. They want their football back. They try to pull the rope. But the rope is stuck. They cannot get their football.

A man sees them. He is kind. He has a ladder. He says to them, "Don't cry, boys. I will help you. I will get your football. But you should not attach your football to the tree. It is not a good idea. It is not nice for the tree or the bird or the football. You should play with your football on the ground. That is where it belongs."

The man climbs the ladder. He gets the football. He gives it to Tom and Sam. He also gives them a patch. He says, "You can fix your football with this patch. It will be like new. But remember, be careful with your things. And respect nature. That is the moral of the story."

Tom and Sam say thank you to the man. They are sorry for what they did. They promise to be careful and respectful. They fix their football with the patch. They play with their football on the ground. They are happy again. They are friends.

Sam and Mia were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they found a baseball in the grass. Sam wanted to throw it and catch it, but Mia wanted to keep it.

"Give me the ball, Mia!" Sam said.

"No, it is mine!" Mia said. "I found it first!"

They pulled and tugged on the ball, but neither of them would let go. They started to yell and cry.

A big girl named Lily saw them and came over. She was older and smarter than Sam and Mia. She knew how to share and be kind.

"What is wrong, little ones?" Lily asked.

"They want my ball!" Mia said.

"No, it is my ball!" Sam said.

Lily looked at the ball and saw something. She smiled and said, "Do you know what this is? This is not a ball. This is a seed. A seed is something that can grow into a flower or a tree or a fruit. If you plant it in the dirt and water it, it will bloom. Bloom means to open up and show pretty colors. Do you want to see it bloom?"

Sam and Mia stopped fighting and looked at the seed. They nodded and said, "Yes, we want to see it bloom!"

Lily took them to a spot where there was some dirt and a hose. She helped them dig a hole and put the seed in it. Then she turned on the hose and let them water the seed.

"There, now you have to be patient," Lily said. "Patient means to wait and not be angry or sad. The seed needs time and sun and rain to grow. Maybe in a few weeks or months, you will see a flower or a tree or a fruit. Then you can both enjoy it and be happy."

Sam and Mia smiled and thanked Lily. They decided to be friends again and play something else. They learned that sharing and being kind was better than fighting and being mean. They also learned about seeds and blooms and patience. They looked forward to seeing what their seed would become.

One day, they found a big jar with a lid. It was heavy and dusty. They wondered what was inside. Tom opened the lid and smelled the jar. He made a sour face and said, "Yuck! This smells bad!" Lily wanted to smell it too. She took the jar from Tom and put it near her nose. She also made a sour face and said, "Ew! This is gross!"

They did not know that the jar had jam in it. But the jam was very old and had mold on it. The mold was green and fuzzy and spread all over the jam. It made the jam smell sour and nasty.

Tom and Lily did not like the jar. They wanted to get rid of it. They looked for a place to put it. They saw a window in the attic. They thought they could throw the jar out of the window. They went to the window and opened it. They saw the garden below. They saw their mom and dad working in the garden. They saw their dog running in the grass.

Tom and Lily did not see the tree near the window. They did not see the branch that was in the way. They threw the jar out of the window. But the jar hit the branch and broke. They heard their mom and dad shout, "What was that?" They heard their dog bark, "Woof!" They looked at each other and said, "Uh-oh!" They knew they were in trouble. They wished they had not found the jar. They wished they had not played in the attic.

But then they heard their mom calling them. She said it was time for lunch. She said she had made their favorite sandwiches and fruit. Lily and Ben felt guilty. Lily liked to grow flowers in her garden. She had many colors and shapes of flowers. She watered them every day and sang to them. She was happy when they grew big and pretty.

She tried to shoo the bug with her hands, but it was too fast and mean. It flew at her face and made her scream. She ran inside the house and told her mom. Her mom gave her a hug and a glass of water. She said, "Don't worry, Lily. The bug can't hurt you. It's just looking for food. But we can help the flowers."

Lily and her mom went back to the garden. They sprayed the flowers and the bug. The bug tried to fly away, but it couldn't. It fell on the ground and crawled away. "Mom, Mom, Ben cut his finger. He touched the razor. It's bleeding," Lily said.

Mom saw Ben's finger. She was worried. But she was also proud of Lily.

"Oh, Ben, you should not touch the razor. It's dangerous. But don't worry, I'll fix it. And Lily, you are very brave. You helped your brother. You are a good sister," Mom said.

"Does it feel better, Ben?" she asked.

"Yes, Mom. I'm sorry. I won't touch the razor again," Ben said.

"Yes, Mom. And me too," Lily said.

Sara and Ben were friends who liked to play with cars. They had many cars of different colors and sizes. One day, they found a new car in the park. It was big and shiny and had a loud horn. Sara and Ben both wanted the car.

"Let me have it!" Sara said.

"No, it's mine!" Ben said.

They pulled and pushed and shouted. They did not share or take turns. They made each other grumpy.

A man came and saw them. He was the owner of the car. He was not happy.

"Hey, kids, that's my car!" he said. "Why are you fighting over it?"

Sara and Ben stopped and looked at him. They felt ashamed.

"We're sorry, mister," Sara said. "We both liked your car and wanted to play with it."

"Well, you can't have it. It's not yours. It's mine. And you shouldn't fight with your friend. That's not nice. You should be kind and respectful. Do you understand?" the man said.

Sara and Ben nodded. They understood.

"Can we play with your car for a little while, please?" Ben asked.

The man thought for a moment. He was not grumpy anymore. He was generous.

"Okay, you can play with it for a little while. But you have to promise me two things. First, you have to share and take turns. Second, you have to give it back to me when I say so. Do you promise?" the man said.

Sara and Ben smiled. They promised.

"Thank you, mister!" they said.

They played with the car happily. They shared and took turns. They did not fight or shout. They had fun.

The man watched them and smiled. He was glad.

After a while, he said, "Okay, kids, time's up. You have to give me back my car now. Do you remember your promise?"

Sara and Ben remembered. They gave him back his car. They thanked him again.

"You're welcome, kids. You're good kids. You kept your promise. I'm proud of you. And I hope you learned something today. What did you learn?" the man said.

Sara and Ben looked at each other. They learned a lot.

"We learned that we should not fight with our friend. We learned that we should share and take turns. We learned that we should keep our promise. And we learned that we should be kind and respectful. Right, Ben?" Sara said.

"Right, Sara. And we learned that your car is awesome, mister. But we don't need it to have fun. We have each other. And we have our own cars. Right, Sara?" Ben said.

"Right, Ben. We have everything we need. And we're happy. Right, mister?" Sara said.

"Right, kids. You're happy. And so am I. You made my day. Now, go and play with your own cars. And remember what you learned. Goodbye, kids!" the man said.

He got in his car and drove away. He honked his horn and waved.

Sara and Ben waved back. They got their own cars and played together. They were not grumpy anymore. They were happy.

Lily was sad that she couldn't go to class, but she listened to the doctor and stayed home. After a few days, Lily felt much better and was excited to go back to class. When she returned, her teacher and classmates were so happy to see her. They had missed her so much! 

Lily learned that it's important to take care of yourself when you're not feeling well, even if it means missing class for a little while. And she was happy to be back with her friends and teacher again.

But the fire was not nice. It burned the trees and the animals. It hurt Ben's eyes and lungs. He started to cough and cry. He wanted to go back home, but he did not know the way.

Then he heard a voice. It was a wise owl who lived in the woods. The owl saw Ben and flew to him. He said, "Little boy, why did you follow the fire? The fire is bad. It can hurt you and the woods. You should stay away from the fire. Come with me, I will show you the way home."

Ben was happy to see the owl. He said, "Thank you, wise owl. I was silly to follow the fire. I will not do it again. Please take me home." The owl nodded and flew ahead. Ben followed the owl as he led him out of the woods.

Soon, Ben saw his house. He ran to his mom and dad and hugged them. He told them what happened and said he was sorry. His mom and dad were angry, but they were also glad that he was safe. They thanked the owl for helping Ben. The owl said, "You are welcome. Remember, little boy, do not follow the fire. Follow the wise." Then he flew away. Eventually Emily heard a voice. It was her mom calling her. Emily replied, "Hi Mom! I'm on the tank! It's fun!" Her mom replied, "Come down right now. It is getting late and you need to come home." 

Emily reluctantly agreed, and started to twist down from the tank. As she did, the metal felt uncomfortable against her hands. When she reached the ground she waved goodbye and ran off towards home. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a bird called Tweety. She was the bravest bird in the sky. Every day, she would fly and soar across the land.

One day, while Tweety was flying, she felt the ground shaking. It was an earthquake! Tweety was scared and she flew really fast back to her nest.

Tweety's friend, Robin, noticed her rushing back home. "What's wrong, Tweety?" he asked.

Tweety was too afraid to answer. She just shook her head and hung her head low.

Robin knew something was up. He flew close to Tweety and said, "It's okay. Don't be sorry, tell me what happened."

"I felt an earthquake," said Tweety with a shaky voice.

"It's okay," said Robin softly. "We'll go back in the sky to soar. Nothing can touch us up there. Come on, let's go!"

So, Tweety and Robin flew back into the sky and soared across the sky until nightfall. Tweety was so thankful for her brave friend.

John ran up to the elderly man and said, "Hi, my name is John." 

The elderly man smiled and said, "Hello, my name is Mr. Tom. What would you like to talk about?" 

John was about to answer but then he remembered he was carrying something in his hands. He held it up and said, "I have a saw. Do you want to see it?" 

The elderly man politely refused and said, "No, thank you John. I don't need a saw." 

John replied, "Ok, I understand." 

The elderly man smiled again and said, "It was nice talking to you, John. I'm glad you stopped to say hello." 

John and his dad continued their walk in the park. John couldn't stop thinking about how nice the elderly man had been. He knew that it was always important to be polite and kind to elderly people.

The old man turned around and said, "It is alright my dear, this is what happens when you get too carried away. We should always know when enough is enough."

The little girl smiled, gave her father a hug and said, "I love you, Daddy." The old man looked at her with a big smile and said, "I love you too, my little one." From that day on, the old man was careful with the rub and kept his kitchen safe from mess.

The moral of this story is that it is important not to get carried away with something. We should be careful and know when enough is enough.

Tom and Lily heard the rhinoceros and ran to him. They saw that he was stuck in the mud and could not move. He looked very upset and scared.

"Don't worry, rhinoceros. We will help you." Lily said, trying to pull him out. But he was too heavy and big.

"OK, I promise," Max said.

They kicked the ball to each other and had fun. But then, a big dog came out of nowhere and ran towards them. It barked loudly and showed its teeth. It wanted their ball.

Lily and Max were scared. They did not know what to do. They held each other's hands and backed away from the dog.

"Help! Help!" they shouted.

A man heard their cries and came to help. He was alert and brave. He had a leash in his hand. He grabbed the dog by the collar and put the leash on it.

"Sorry, kids. This is my dog. He escaped from the yard. He likes to chase balls, but he doesn't mean to hurt you," the man said.

He gave the ball back to Lily and Max and apologized again.

"Thank you, mister. You saved us," Lily said.

"Yes, thank you. You are very kind," Max said.

They hugged the man and then ran back to their home. They were happy to be safe and to have their ball.

They learned to be careful when they played in the park. They always stayed near the fence and watched out for dogs. They also kept their promise to each other. They were good friends.

Sam was a big boy. He was three years old. He had a red bike. He loved his bike. He rode it every day in the park.

One day, Sam saw a hill. He wanted to go down the hill on his bike. He thought it would be fun. He did not see the rocks and the sticks on the hill. He did not know it was a rough hill.

Sam pedaled fast and went down the hill. He felt the wind in his hair. He felt happy. But then he hit a rock. His bike bounced and shook. Sam lost his balance. He fell off his bike. He scraped his knee and his elbow. He cried.

Mom came running. She saw Sam on the ground. She saw his bike on the side. She saw the blood on his knee and his elbow. She felt sad. She hugged Sam and said, "It's okay, my sweet boy. You are brave. You will be fine."

She took Sam to the car. She put a band-aid on his knee and his elbow. She gave him a kiss and a cookie. She said, "You had a rough day, Sam. But you learned something. Next time, be careful on the hill. Look for the rocks and the sticks. They can hurt you and your bike."

Sam nodded. He felt better. He said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I love you. I love my bike. Can I ride it again tomorrow?"

Mom smiled. She said, "Of course, Sam. You can ride your bike again tomorrow. But only on the flat path. And wear your helmet. It will protect your head."

Sam agreed. He said, "Okay, Mom. I will. Thank you for helping me. You are the best mom in the world."

Mom and Sam drove home. They had a good year. They had many adventures. But they never went down the rough hill again.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play with colors. They have red, blue, yellow and green paints. They use brushes to make pictures on paper.

One day, Sara has an idea. She says, "Let's mix colors and see what happens." Ben nods and smiles. They start to mix red and blue. They get purple. They mix yellow and blue. They get green. They mix red and yellow. They get orange.

They are happy with their new colors. They make more pictures with them. They show each other their work.

But then, Sara sees Ben's picture. He has mixed all the colors together. He has made brown. Sara likes brown. She thinks it is a nice color. She is jealous of Ben's picture. She says, "Hey, that's not fair. You used all the colors. You broke the law. The law is, you can only mix two colors at a time."

Ben is confused. He says, "What law? I just wanted to see what happens. I like brown. It is a different color. You can make brown too. There is enough paint for both of us."

Sara is angry. She says, "No, you can't make brown. Brown is mine. You have to give me your picture. Or I will tell the teacher."

Ben is scared. He likes his picture. He does not want to give it to Sara. He does not want to get in trouble. He says, "No, please. Don't tell the teacher. This is my picture. I made it. You can make your own brown. Please, Sara. Be nice."

Sara and Ben start to argue. They raise their voices. They pull each other's pictures. They make a mess. The teacher hears them. She comes to see what is wrong. She sees the paint, the paper, and the tears. She is not happy. She says, "Sara, Ben, what are you doing? Why are you fighting? Why are you wasting the paint? Why are you ruining your pictures?"

Sara and Ben stop. They look at the teacher. They look at each other. They feel ashamed. They say, "Sorry, teacher. Sorry, Sara. Sorry, Ben."

The teacher says, "It's okay. I'm glad you are sorry. But you need to learn to share and respect each other. There is no law about mixing colors. You can mix as many as you want. But you have to be careful and clean. And you have to be kind and polite. Do you understand?"

Sara and Ben nod. They say, "Yes, teacher. We understand."

The teacher says, "Good. Now, let's clean up this mess. And then, let's make some new pictures. And let's use all the colors. Because all the colors are beautiful. And so are you."

Lila and Tom were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big slide that looked very fun. Lila wanted to try it, but Tom was scared. He said, "No, no, Lila, it is too high and too fast. We might fall and hurt ourselves."

Lila urged Tom to be brave and join her. She said, "Come on, Tom, it is not so bad. We can hold hands and go together. It will be a lot of fun. Don't be scared, be strong."

Tom was not sure, but he did not want to let Lila down. He nodded and followed her to the slide. They climbed up the steps and sat on the top. Lila smiled and said, "Ready, set, go!" and pushed them down the slide.

They zoomed down the slide, feeling the wind in their hair and the sun on their faces. They laughed and screamed with joy. They reached the bottom and landed on a soft mat. They looked at each other and hugged. They felt very happy and proud.

But then, they saw a surprise. Their mom was waiting for them with a big cake and balloons. She said, "Happy birthday, Lila and Tom! I am so proud of you for trying something new and having fun. You are very brave and kind to each other. I love you very much."

Lila and Tom were so happy that they forgot their fear. They ran to their mom and hugged her. They thanked her for the surprise and the cake. They shared it with their friends and had a great party. They learned that sometimes, it is good to try new things and face your fears. You might find something fun and wonderful. And you always have your family and friends to support you.

Tom and Lily were playing in the sandbox. They had a lot of toys, but they both wanted the same truck. It was big and red and had four wheels.

"Give me the truck!" Tom said. He tried to grab it from Lily.

"No, it's mine!" Lily said. She held the truck tight.

They pulled and pushed and shouted. They were not happy.

Sam saw them and came over. He had a bucket and a shovel. He liked to build things in the sand.

"Hi, Tom and Lily. What are you doing?" he asked.

"We are fighting over the truck!" Tom said.

"That's not fun. Why don't you share the truck?" Sam said.

"Share? How?" Lily asked.

"Well, you can take turns driving the truck. Or you can use it together to build something. Like a castle or a bridge or a road," Sam said.

He showed them how to fill the bucket with sand and dump it on the ground. He used the shovel to make shapes and patterns.

"Wow, that looks cool!" Tom said.

"Yeah, that's fun!" Lily said.

They decided to stop fighting and join Sam. They used the truck to carry sand and make a big castle. They put a flag on top and a moat around it.

They were very happy. They thanked Sam for being generous and helping them.

"Can we be your friends?" Tom and Lily asked.

"Of course! You are my friends. Friends share and build things together," Sam said.

They smiled and hugged. They played in the sandbox until it was time to go home.

Lily and Ben were playing pirates in the garden. They had a big box that they pretended was a treasure chest. They filled it with shiny things and old toys. They took turns to guard the chest and look for enemies.

"Ahoy, matey!" Ben said, holding a wooden sword. "I see a ship on the horizon. It must be the bad pirates. They want to steal our treasure!"

"Oh no!" Lily said, grabbing a plastic binoculars. "We have to stop them. Do we have enough supplies to fight them?"

Ben opened the chest and looked inside. He saw some crackers, some juice boxes, some band-aids and some stickers. He smiled and said, "Yes, we do. We have good supplies. We can share them with our friends and make them strong. Then we can scare away the bad pirates with our swords and our shouts."

Lily nodded and said, "Good idea. Let's call our friends and make a plan. We are the good pirates. We protect our treasure and our friends."

They ran to the house and asked their mom if they could invite some friends over. Their mom said yes and helped them make some invitations. They wrote, "Come to our pirate party. Bring your sword and your hat. We have a treasure chest and good supplies. Arrr!" They gave the invitations to their friends and waited for them to come. They were excited to play pirates and have fun.

Sara and Tom were playing on the beach. They liked to run and jump in the sand. They saw a big wave coming from the sea. Sara wanted to go closer and see the water. Tom was scared and said no.

"Come on, Tom, it is fun!" Sara said. "The wave is not bad. It is just water."

"No, Sara, it is too big and too loud. It can hurt us. We should stay here." Tom said. He was stubborn and did not want to move.

Sara did not listen to Tom. She ran towards the wave. She was not careful and did not see a rock. She stumbled on the rock and fell down. The wave reached her and splashed her. She was wet and cold and cried.

Tom heard Sara cry and ran to help her. He was sorry for her and hugged her. He said, "I am sorry, Sara. Are you okay? The wave was too strong. You should have listened to me."

Sara nodded and said, "I am sorry, Tom. You were right. The wave was too big and too loud. It hurt me. You are a good friend. Can we go back and play in the sand?"

Tom smiled and said, "Yes, Sara. We can go back and play in the sand. But next time, be careful and do not run to the wave. It is dangerous."

Sara and Tom held hands and walked back to the sand. They played and laughed and forgot about the wave. They were happy.

Tom and Sue were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. The sun was mild and the air was fresh. They saw some mist near the pond. They wanted to see what it was.

"Look, mist!" Tom said. "Let's go there!"

"OK!" Sue said. "But we have to finish our snack first."

They ate their apple and cheese quickly. Then they ran to the pond. The mist was soft and cool. They touched it with their hands. They laughed and made funny shapes.

"Hello, mist!" Tom said. "You are nice!"

"Hello, children!" a voice said. "You are nice too!"

Tom and Sue looked around. They saw a duck in the pond. It was the duck that spoke.

"Wow, a talking duck!" Sue said. "How can you talk?"

"I can talk because I am magic!" the duck said. "I live in the mist. It gives me powers. Do you want to play with me?"

"Yes, please!" Tom and Sue said. They were very happy. They played with the duck and the mist. They had a lot of fun. They forgot about the time.

Lily liked to sing. She sang all the time. She sang in the morning, she sang at lunch, she sang at night. She sang loud and she sang soft. She sang happy and she sang sad. She sang songs she knew and songs she made up.

When the opera started, Lily saw people on the stage. They were singing too, but not like Lily. They sang very high and very low. They sang in a language Lily did not understand. They sang with music and costumes and lights. Lily thought they were very good. She clapped her hands and smiled.

One of the people on the stage was a lady with a long dress and a big voice. She was the star of the opera. She was famous. Everyone loved her. Lily loved her too. She wanted to be like her.

At the end of the opera, the lady came to the front of the stage. She bowed and smiled. She saw Lily in the front row. She waved at her and said, "Hello, little girl. Do you like to sing?"

Anna liked to help her mom bake pastries. Pastries were sweet and yummy things that you could eat for breakfast or as a treat. Anna's mom would let her mix the flour, the butter, the sugar and the eggs in a big bowl. Then she would roll out the dough and cut out shapes with a cookie cutter. Anna liked to make stars, hearts and circles.

One day, Anna's mom had to go to the store to buy some milk. She told Anna to stay in the kitchen and watch the pastries in the oven. She said she would be back soon. Anna nodded and said okay. She was a good girl and she did not want to make her mom mad.

But after a while, Anna got bored. The pastries looked dull and brown in the oven. They did not smell good anymore. Anna wondered what would happen if she added some more sugar and some sprinkles. She thought that would make them more fun and tasty. She found a jar of sugar and a box of sprinkles in the cupboard. She opened the oven and took out the baking tray. She sprinkled some sugar and some sprinkles on the pastries. She thought they looked much better. She put the tray back in the oven and closed the door.

She did not know that the sugar and the sprinkles would start to burn and make smoke. She did not know that the smoke would set off the fire alarm. She did not know that the fire alarm would make a loud noise and scare her. She did not know that her mom would come back and see the mess and be very angry.

She only knew that she wanted to make the pastries more fun and tasty. She only knew that she made a big mistake. She only knew that she was sorry.

Anna and Ben were going on a trip with Mom and Dad. They packed their luggage with clothes, toys and books. They were very excited to see new places and have fun.

They got in the car and drove to the airport. Anna and Ben looked out the window and saw many things. They saw big trucks, tall buildings, green trees and blue sky. They asked Mom and Dad many questions about what they saw.

"Mom, what is that?" Anna pointed to a big plane.

"That is a plane, Anna. We will go on a plane soon. It will take us to our destination." Mom said.

"Wow, a plane! Can I fly it?" Ben asked.

"No, Ben. Only the pilot can fly the plane. He knows how to do it. You can watch him from your seat." Dad said.

They arrived at the airport and got out of the car. They took their luggage and walked to the check-in counter. There was a long line of people waiting to check in their luggage. Anna and Ben were bored and restless. They started to run around and play tag.

"Stop, stop!" Mom and Dad said. "You have to stay with us. It is not safe to run around here. There are many people and things that can hurt you."

"But we want to play!" Anna and Ben said. "We are tired of waiting!"

"I know, I know. But you have to be patient. We will check in soon and then we can go to the gate. There will be a play area there. You can play there while we wait for our plane." Mom said.

"OK, OK. We will stop." Anna and Ben said. They came back to Mom and Dad and held their hands.

"Sorry, sorry. I made a mistake. This is not my backpack." The man said. He gave the backpack back to Ben.

"Thank you, thank you." Ben said. He hugged his backpack. He was glad to have it back. It had his favorite toy and book inside.

They went to the gate and found the play area. Anna and Ben played with the toys and slides. They made new friends and had fun. Mom and Dad watched them and smiled.

"Come on, kids. It's time to go. Our plane is ready." Mom said.

"Yay, yay! Let's go, let's go!" Anna and Ben said. They grabbed their backpacks and followed Mom and Dad.

They boarded the plane and found their seats. They buckled their seat belts and listened to the safety instructions. They looked out the window and saw the plane move and take off.

They were on their way to Hawaii. They were happy and excited. They wondered what they would see and do there.

They hoped there would be yummy food and drinks, beautiful beaches and flowers, and lots of fun and adventure.

One day, a brown bear was looking for food in the forest. He was very hungry and tired. He saw a big fish in the river and wanted to catch it. He jumped into the water and tried to bite the fish, but the fish was too fast and swam away.

The bear was angry and wet. He climbed out of the river and shook his fur. He saw a man with a spear standing on the other side. The man was hunting for animals. He saw the bear and raised his spear to throw it.

The bear was scared and ran away. He ran and ran until he found a cave. He went inside the cave and saw that it was dark and quiet. He felt safe and warm. He decided to rest in the cave until the man was gone.

He lay down on the ground and closed his eyes. He heard a voice in the cave. It was another bear. The other bear said, "Who are you? Why are you in my cave?"

The brown bear opened his eyes and saw a black bear. The black bear was bigger and stronger than him. He said, "I'm sorry. I was running from a man with a spear. He wanted to hurt me. Can I rest here for a while?"

The black bear looked at the brown bear and saw that he was hungry and tired. He felt sorry for him. He said, "OK. You can rest here for a while. But you have to share some food with me later. I have some honey and berries in the back of the cave."

The brown bear nodded and said, "Thank you. You are very kind. I will share some food with you later." He smiled and closed his eyes again. He rested in the cave with the black bear. He felt happy and safe. He made a new friend.

Tommy was a little boy who liked to talk a lot. He talked to his mom, his dad, his sister, his toys, and even his dog. He talked when he was happy, when he was sad, when he was bored, and when he was curious. He talked so much that sometimes he forgot to listen.

The girl looked at him and said, "No, thank you. I don't feel like playing. My stomach hurts."

Tommy was surprised. He didn't know what to say. He wanted to help her, but he didn't know how. He thought for a moment, and then he said, "I'm sorry your stomach hurts. Do you want me to get you some water? Or a hug?"

The girl smiled a little. She said, "That's very kind of you. A hug would be nice."

Tommy gave her a big hug. He felt her stomach rumble. He said, "Maybe you're hungry. Do you want to share my snack? I have some crackers and cheese."

Tommy said, "It means you care about other people and want to help them. My mom taught me that word. She says it's important to be compassionate."

The girl said, "I'm Lily. Nice to meet you, Tommy."

Ben and Mia were twins who liked to play in their room. They had many toys and books and games, but sometimes they got bored and restless. They wanted to explore new things and have fun.

One day, they saw a shiny thing on the table in the living room. It was round and silver and had some black stuff inside. They wondered what it was and how it felt. They decided to sneak out of their room and go to the table.

"Look, Ben, it's an ashtray!" Mia said. She had heard their dad say that word before. He used to smoke and put his cigarettes in the ashtray, but he stopped because mom said it was bad for him.

"Can I touch it?" Ben asked. He was curious and wanted to see if the black stuff was soft or hard.

"OK, but be careful. Don't make any noise or mom will hear us," Mia said. She looked around and saw that mom was busy in the kitchen. She reached for the ashtray and lifted it up.

"Wow, it's heavy!" she said. She tried to balance it in her hand, but it was too big and slippery. She dropped it on the floor and it made a loud clang.

"Uh-oh!" Ben said. He saw the ashtray break into pieces and the black stuff scatter everywhere. He also saw mom come out of the kitchen and look at them with a frown.

"What are you doing, kids?" mom asked. She was angry and worried. She knew the ashtray was sharp and the black stuff was dirty. She did not want them to get hurt or make a mess.

"Sorry, mom, we were just playing," Mia said. She felt guilty and scared. She knew they had done something wrong.

"Playing with what? The ashtray? That's not a toy, that's a dangerous thing. You could have cut yourself or swallowed the ashtray. You know you're not supposed to touch dad's things. Go to your room right now and think about what you did," mom said. She picked up the broken ashtray and the black stuff and threw them in the trash. She was disappointed and sad. She wished they had listened to her.

One day, Lily and Sam go to the park with their moms. They see something new in the park. It is a big purple balloon. The balloon is tied to a basket. The basket has a man and a woman inside. They are smiling and waving.

"Wow, look at that!" Lily says.

"What is it?" Sam asks.

"It is a balloon. It can fly in the sky," Lily says.

"Can we fly in the balloon too?" Sam asks.

"I don't know. Let's ask the man and the woman," Lily says.

They run to the basket. They say hello to the man and the woman.

"Hello, kids. Do you like our balloon?" the man asks.

"Yes, we do. It is very big and purple. Can we fly in the balloon too?" Lily asks.

"Sorry, kids. The balloon is not for kids. It is only for grown-ups. It is too high and too fast for kids," the woman says.

"Oh, that's too bad. We wanted to fly in the sky and see the park from above," Sam says.

"Maybe when you are older, you can fly in a balloon. But for now, you can enjoy the park on the ground. There are many fun things to do in the park," the man says.

"Okay, thank you. Have a nice flight," Lily says.

"Bye, bye. Be careful and have fun," the woman says.

The man and the woman untie the balloon. The balloon goes up in the sky. Lily and Sam wave goodbye. They go back to their moms. They tell them about the balloon. They play in the park. They have a good time. They are happy.

"See? The dog is friendly. It likes me," Anna says.

Ben is still scared. He stays behind. He watches Anna and the dog.

"Anna, be careful," Ben says. "The dog might hurt you. Come back here."

"Ben, come here. The dog is fun. It won't hurt you. I promise," Anna says.

"Look, Sam, this is our map!" Lily said, holding up her paper. "We can use it to play hide and seek. You can be the seeker and I can be the hider. You have to follow the map to find me."

"OK, Lily, that sounds fun!" Sam said, taking the map. "You can hide anywhere you want, but don't go too far. I will count to ten and then look for you."

Lily ran away to find a good hiding spot. She looked at the map and saw a charming spot. It was behind the shed, where there was a pile of leaves. She thought Sam would not see her there. She crawled under the leaves and waited.

Sam counted to ten and then looked at the map. He saw the big tree, the swing, the sandbox, and the shed. He wondered where Lily was. He decided to start with the shed. He walked around it and saw something moving under the leaves. He smiled and said, "I found you, Lily! You are a good hider, but I am a good seeker. I used the map to find you."

Lily came out of the leaves and laughed. She said, "You are right, Sam, you are a good seeker. And we are good designers. Our map is awesome. Let's play again!"

Anna and Ben are playing in the snow. They make a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They want to give him a nose, but they do not have a carrot.

"Look, Ben, I have an idea!" Anna says. She runs to the house and comes back with a pink ice pop. "We can use this as a nose!"

Ben likes the idea. He takes the ice pop and sticks it on the snowman's face. The snowman looks funny and happy.

"Wow, he is the best snowman ever!" Ben says. He gives Anna a hug.

But then they hear a loud noise. It is a big truck. The truck is coming to load the snow and take it away.

"Oh no, the truck will take our snowman!" Anna cries. She and Ben run to the snowman and try to protect him.

"Please, mister, do not take our snowman!" they shout. "He is our friend!"

The truck driver sees the children and the snowman. He smiles and stops the truck.

"Hello, kids, what a nice snowman you have!" he says. "I like his pink nose. Do not worry, I will not take him. I will only take the snow around him. He can stay with you."

Anna and Ben are happy. They thank the truck driver and wave to him. They stay with their snowman and share the ice pop with him. They think he is the best snowman ever.

The acorns are for the squirrels. They need them for food. If you take them, the squirrels will be sad and hungry."

Sara did not listen to Ben. She said, "I don't care about the squirrels. I like the acorns. They are shiny and brown. I want to keep them for myself." She picked up some acorns and ran away from Ben.

Ben followed Sara and tried to stop her. He said, "Sara, please, give back the acorns. It is not nice to take things that are not yours. You have to share and be kind. That is what Mom and Dad taught us."

Sara did not listen to Ben. She said, "No, Ben, you are silly. The acorns are mine. I found them first. You can't tell me what to do." She ran faster and faster.

But Sara did not see where she was going. She ran into a big rock and fell down. She hurt her knee and her hand. She dropped the acorns and they rolled away. She started to cry.

Ben came to Sara and helped her up. He said, "Sara, are you okay? I'm sorry you got hurt. Here, let me give you a hug." He hugged Sara and wiped her tears.

Sara felt sorry for what she did. She said, "Ben, I'm sorry too. I was wrong. I should not have taken the acorns. I should have listened to you. You are a good brother. Can you forgive me?"

Ben smiled and said, "Of course, Sara, I forgive you. You are a good sister. Come on, let's go back to the tree and put the acorns back. Maybe we can see some squirrels and say sorry to them too."

Sara and Ben walked back to the tree and put the acorns back. They saw some squirrels and waved to them. The squirrels waved back and thanked them. Sara and Ben felt happy and proud. They learned a lesson. They learned to respect nature and animals. They learned to be honest and generous. They learned to love each other.

"You're welcome, Lily. It is fun to discover new things with you," Ben said, smiling back. They walked back to their mom, holding their stones and their hands. They were happy and curious. They wondered what else they could discover in the world.

Lila was lost and scared, and did not know what to do. She sat down in the snow, and hugged herself. She hoped that someone would find her, and take her home. But no one came. She was alone, and cold, and shivering. She closed her eyes, and did not open them again.

The moral of the story is: You should be nice and share your stuff with your sister or brother, and listen to your mom when she tells you to wear warm clothes. If you are not, you might lose your sister or brother, and get very cold and sick. You should love your sister or brother, and help them when they need you. They are your family, and they are important.

"Hello, I am Robo. I am a friendly robot. I came from a far away place. I need your help. My battery is weak. Can you please share the cube and charge me?" the robot said.

Lila and Tom stopped fighting. They were very surprised and curious. They had never seen a robot before.

"A robot?" Lila said. "Wow, that is amazing!"

"How can we help you?" Tom said. "What do you need?"

The robot smiled. It showed them a small hole on its chest. It said that the cube was its charger. It needed to plug the cube into the hole to get energy.

Lila and Tom felt sorry for the robot. They decided to share the cube and help the robot. They took turns to plug the cube into the robot's chest. The robot thanked them and told them stories about its home and adventures.

Lila and Tom became friends with the robot. They learned many new things from it. They also learned to share and be kind. They had a lot of fun with the robot and the cube.

"Did you have fun playing with Spot?" she asked. Tim smiled and said, "Yes, Mom! We had lots of fun. I'm glad I didn't join you for the boring work upstairs."

Tim's mom laughed and said, "I'm glad you had fun, Tim. Now, let's all have dinner together." And they did.

Tom had an idea. He went to find water for the car. He put the water in the car. The car felt happy. Tom tried to turn the car on again. This time, the engine went. The car and Tom were happy and went home.

Lily was a little girl who liked to run and play. She was eager to join the big kids in their games, but they said she was too small and slow. Lily felt sad and wished she could gain some speed and size.

One day, she saw a shiny red bike in the store window. She asked her mom if she could have it. Her mom said yes, but only if she saved her money and did her chores. Lily agreed and worked hard to earn the bike. She counted her coins every night and dreamed of riding the bike.

After many weeks, Lily had enough money to buy the bike. She was so happy and proud. She thanked her mom and ran to the store with her. She picked the bike and put on a helmet. She was ready to ride.

She pedaled fast and felt the wind in her hair. She saw the big kids playing in the park. She wanted to show them her bike and join them. She rode towards them, but did not see a big rock on the road. She hit the rock and fell off the bike. She scraped her knee and hurt her foot. She cried and called for her mom.

Her mom came and hugged her. She cleaned her wound and put a band-aid on it. She said, "I'm sorry, Lily. Are you okay?"

Lily nodded and sniffed. She said, "I'm okay, mom. But I was so eager to ride the bike and play with the big kids. I did not look where I was going. I was silly."

Her mom smiled and said, "It's okay, Lily. You were excited and happy. But you also learned a lesson. You have to be careful and watch out for dangers. You have to balance your eagerness with your safety. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I will be more careful next time. Can I still ride the bike?"

Her mom said, "Of course, you can. But only when your foot feels better. And only with me or dad. And always wear your helmet. Okay?"

Lily said, "Okay, mom. Thank you. I love you."

Her mom said, "I love you too, Lily. You are a brave and smart girl. And you have a beautiful bike. Come on, let's go home and rest your foot."

They walked home, holding the bike and each other's hand. Lily felt better and smiled. She was happy to have the bike and her mom. She was eager to ride again, but also careful to avoid rocks. She had gained more than speed and size. She had gained wisdom and love.

"Ow! The pine tree hurt me!" Lily cried.

"I'm sorry, Lily. Do you want a hug?" Tom asked.

"Yes, please." Lily said.

Tom hugged Lily. He tried to make her feel better.

"Maybe we can find something else to play with. Something that doesn't hurt." Tom said.

"Look, Tom. A sandwich. Can we eat it?" Lily asked.

Tom looked at the sandwich. He felt hungry.

"I don't know, Lily. It's not ours. Maybe someone left it here. Maybe they will come back for it." Tom said.

Lily shrugged. She didn't care. She was hungry too.

"I don't think so, Tom. It's been here for a long time. No one is coming back for it. Let's eat it. It's better than the pine tree." Lily said.

She grabbed the sandwich. She broke it in half. She gave one half to Tom. She took the other half. She bit into it. It was tasty. She smiled.

"Yum! This is a good sandwich. Thank you, pine tree." Lily said.

Tom bit into his half. He agreed.

"Yum! This is a good sandwich. Thank you, pine tree." Tom said.

They ate the sandwich. They felt happy. They forgot about the pain. They thanked the pine tree. They didn't know that the sandwich belonged to a man who was sleeping on the grass. He woke up and saw them. He was angry. He shouted at them.

"Hey! That's my sandwich! Give it back!" He said.

But it was too late. The sandwich was gone. Lily and Tom ran away. They laughed. They had fun. They didn't like the pine tree. But they liked the sandwich.

One day, a little boy named Ben went to the zoo with his mom and dad. He liked to see all the different animals, but his favorite was the rhinoceros. He thought it was very big and strong, and he liked its horn.

He ran to the fence where the rhinoceros was and stared at it with his big eyes. He wanted to touch it and play with it, but his mom said no. She said it was not safe, and that the rhinoceros might get angry or scared.

"Why?" Ben asked. "He looks nice and friendly. He is not mean like the lion or the snake."

"Because he is wild, Ben," his dad said. "He is not used to people, and he might hurt you by accident. He needs his space and his peace. You can look at him, but you have to respect him."

Ben nodded, but he still felt curious. He wondered what the rhinoceros felt like, and what he ate, and what he did at night. He wished he could be his friend.

When it was time to go home, Ben said goodbye to the rhinoceros and waved his hand. He hoped the rhinoceros would remember him and be happy.

But as he turned around, he saw something that made him stop. It was getting dark, and the zoo was closing. The rhinoceros was alone in his enclosure, with no other animals or people around. He looked sad and lonely, and he stared at the ground.

Ben felt sorry for him. He realized that the rhinoceros was not free, and that he missed his home and his family. He understood that the zoo was not the best place for him, and that he deserved to live in the wild, where he belonged.

He ran back to his mom and dad and hugged them. He said, "I love you, and I'm glad we are together. I hope the rhinoceros can find his home and his friends too. He needs them more than me."

His mom and dad smiled and kissed him. They said, "We love you too, Ben. And we are proud of you. You are a kind and smart boy. You have learned a very important lesson today. You have learned to care for others, and to respect their needs and feelings. That is what makes a good friend."

The end.

One day, Lily spun in the library. She spun around the books, the chairs, and the people. She spun and spun and spun. She did not see the sign that said "Quiet, please".

The librarian saw Lily. She was not happy. She said, "Stop, Lily, stop! You are making too much noise. You are bothering the other people. You are not being good. You need a lecture."

Lily stopped spinning. She felt sad. She did not like lectures. Lectures were long and boring. Lectures made her feel bad. She said, "I'm sorry, librarian. I did not mean to be bad. I just like to spin. Spinning is fun."

The librarian looked at Lily. She saw that Lily was sorry. She saw that Lily was a little girl who liked to spin. She said, "I understand, Lily. Spinning is fun. But not in the library. The library is for reading and learning. The library is a quiet place. You can spin somewhere else. Like in the park. The park is a light and open place. You can spin and play and laugh in the park. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, librarian. I understand. I will not spin in the library anymore. I will spin in the park. Thank you for telling me. Can I still read a book?"

The librarian smiled. She said, "Of course, Lily. You can still read a book. Reading is good for you. Reading can make you happy and smart. Reading can take you to many places. Even places where you can spin. Here, take this book. It is about a girl who likes to spin. Maybe you will like it."

"Can we eat it?" Ben asked.

"I don't know. Maybe we should ask someone first," Lily said.

Lily was sad. She wanted to try the jelly too. She asked Ben to share. But Ben said no. He said it was his jelly. He ate more and more. He did not care about Lily.

The end.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big yard with a swing, a slide and a sandbox. They also had a dog named Spot who was very lively and loved to run and jump.

One day, their mom told them to wear their helmets and buckle them up before they went to play. She said it was for their safety, in case they fell or bumped their heads. Tom and Lily nodded, but they did not really listen. They thought helmets were boring and buckles were hard to do.

They ran outside with Spot and had fun on the swing and the slide. Then they decided to go to the sandbox and make a castle. They left their helmets on the grass and forgot about them. Spot saw the helmets and thought they were toys. He grabbed one with his teeth and ran away, wagging his tail.

"Hey, that's my helmet!" Tom shouted, and chased after Spot. Lily followed him, leaving the sandbox and the castle. They ran across the yard, trying to catch Spot, but he was too fast and lively. He dodged and darted, making them trip and tumble.

Suddenly, Spot stopped and dropped the helmet. He barked and wagged his tail, as if he wanted to play. Tom and Lily reached him and saw why he stopped. There was a big hole in the fence, and a busy road on the other side. Cars and trucks zoomed by, making loud noises and smoke.

Tom and Lily felt scared. They knew they were not supposed to go near the road. It was dangerous and they could get hurt. They wished they had their helmets and buckles on, like their mom told them. They grabbed Spot and ran back to the yard, holding him tight.

They found their mom waiting for them, with a worried look on her face. She saw the hole in the fence, the helmet in Spot's mouth, and the dirt and grass on Tom and Lily's clothes. She hugged them and said, "I'm so glad you're safe. You should always wear your helmets and buckle them up when you play outside. You never know what might happen. And you should never go near the road. It's not a place for children or dogs."

Tom and Lily felt sorry and ashamed. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We didn't listen to you. We thought helmets and buckles were boring and hard. But we learned our lesson. They are important and good. We will always wear them and buckle them up from now on. And we will never go near the road again. We love you, mom."

Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Tom and Lily. And I love you, Spot. You're a good dog, even if you're a lively one. Now, let's go inside and have some cookies. And then we'll fix the fence and the helmets."

Tom and Lily nodded and smiled. They followed their mom inside, with Spot behind them. They were happy and grateful. They learned to listen to their mom and to be careful and safe. They also learned to appreciate their helmets and buckles, and their lively dog.

Tom and Ann went to the farm with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like cows, pigs, chickens and sheep. They wanted to feed them and pet them, but Mom and Dad said they had to be careful and gentle.

They came to a pen where there was a goat. The goat had long horns, a beard and a bell around its neck. It looked wild and angry. Tom and Ann were scared of the goat, but they wanted to see it closer.

"Hello, goat," Tom said. "Can we feed you some grass?"

The goat did not answer. It stared at Tom and Ann with its big eyes. It did not like strangers. It wanted to be left alone.

"Maybe it is hungry," Ann said. "Let's give it some grass."

She reached out her hand with some grass, but the goat did not take it. Instead, it sneezed loudly and shook its head. The sneeze was so strong that it blew the grass away and made Ann fall back.

"Ouch!" Ann cried. "The goat sneezed on me!"

Tom ran to help Ann. He was angry at the goat. He wanted to yell at it, but Mom and Dad came and stopped him.

"Don't be mad, Tom," Mom said. "The goat was just trying to protect itself. It is not used to people. It is a wild goat."

"A wild goat?" Tom asked. "Why is it here?"

Dad explained that the goat was rescued from the woods, where it was hurt and hungry. The farmer took it to the farm to heal it and take care of it. But the goat did not trust anyone. It was afraid and lonely.

"Maybe we can be its friends," Ann said. "Maybe we can make it happy."

Mom and Dad smiled. They said that was a nice idea, but they had to be patient and gentle. They had to respect the goat's feelings and space. They had to show it kindness and love.

Tom and Ann nodded. They said they were sorry for bothering the goat. They said they wanted to be its friends. They said they hoped it would feel better soon.

The goat heard them. It looked at them with its big eyes. It did not sneeze this time. It made a soft sound, like a bleat. It was a thank you.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the children to be respectful and compassionate towards animals, especially those who are wild, hurt or scared. It also shows them how to apologize and make friends.

Tommy was a rabbit who loved to eat carrots. He ate them every day for breakfast, lunch and dinner. He had a big pile of carrots in his hole that he dug under the tree. He was very happy and healthy.

One day, a fox came to the tree. He smelled the carrots and wanted to eat them. He dug a hole next to Tommy's hole and sneaked inside. He saw the pile of carrots and started to take them one by one. He did not care about Tommy or his feelings.

Tommy heard a noise in his hole and went to check. He saw the fox with his mouth full of carrots. He was very angry and scared. He said, "Stop! Those are my carrots! Go away!"

The fox laughed and said, "No, they are mine now. You have too many carrots. You are greedy and selfish. I will eat them all and leave you nothing."

Tommy felt very sad and hurt. He did not know what to do. He needed his carrots to live. He started to cry.

Lily was a mouse who lived in the tree. She was Tommy's friend. She was very kind and dependable. She heard Tommy's cry and came to help. She saw the fox and the carrots and understood the problem. She said, "Fox, you are mean and bad. You are stealing Tommy's carrots. You are making him suffer. You should share and be nice."

The fox snarled and said, "Mouse, you are small and weak. You cannot tell me what to do. You should go away or I will eat you too."

Lily was not afraid. She had a plan. She said, "Fox, you are foolish and proud. You think you are smart and strong. But you are not. I have a challenge for you. If you win, you can have all the carrots. If you lose, you have to give them back to Tommy and say sorry."

The fox was curious and confident. He said, "What is the challenge?"

Lily said, "The challenge is to see who can eat the most carrots in one minute. You can use your teeth and claws. I can only use my teeth. Are you ready?"

The fox agreed. He thought he could easily beat the mouse. He did not know that Lily had a trick. She had hidden some hot peppers among the carrots. She knew that foxes hated hot peppers and rabbits loved them.

They started the challenge. The fox grabbed a carrot and bit into it. He felt a burning sensation in his mouth. He spat out the carrot and coughed. He grabbed another carrot and bit into it. He felt the same pain. He spat out the carrot and cried. He grabbed another carrot and bit into it. He felt the same agony. He spat out the carrot and screamed.

Lily grabbed a carrot and bit into it. She felt a sweet and crunchy taste. She swallowed the carrot and smiled. She grabbed another carrot and bit into it. She felt the same delight. She swallowed the carrot and winked. She grabbed another carrot and bit into it. She felt the same joy. She swallowed the carrot and cheered.

The minute was over. Lily had eaten ten carrots. The fox had eaten none. He had only hot peppers in his mouth. He was very unhappy and miserable.

Lily said, "Fox, you have lost the challenge. You have to give back the carrots to Tommy and say sorry."

The fox nodded and did as he was told. He gave back the carrots to Tommy and said, "Sorry, Tommy. I was wrong to take your carrots. You are not greedy and selfish. You are generous and good. I will not bother you again."

Tommy forgave the fox and thanked Lily. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are my friend. You are kind and dependable. You are clever and brave. You have saved my carrots and me."

Lily hugged Tommy and said, "You are welcome, Tommy. You are my friend. You are happy and healthy. You are strong and gentle. You have shared your carrots and me."

They ate some carrots together and laughed. They were very happy and grateful. They had learned a lesson and made a peace.

"Look, Ben, I am making rice!" she said proudly.

"Can I have some rice, Lila?" he asked.

Lila shook her head. "No, Ben, this is my rice. You have to make your own food."

Ben felt sad and angry. He wanted to share with Lila, but she was being mean. He looked around and saw a wooden spoon. He had an idea.

He grabbed the spoon and ran to the pot. He tried to stir the rice, but it was too hot and sticky. He burned his hand and dropped the spoon. The rice spilled over the pot and onto the stove. It made a loud hissing sound and a lot of smoke.

Lila and Ben both screamed. They were scared and hurt. They ran away from the stove and hugged each other.

Mommy heard the noise and came into the kitchen. She saw the mess and the smoke and the crying children. She turned off the stove and opened the window. She was angry and worried.

"What happened here?" she asked.

Mommy sighed. She took them to the sink and washed their hands. She put some ice on Ben's burn and gave them both a hug.

"Listen, Lila and Ben, you have to be careful in the kitchen. The stove is hot and dangerous. You can't play with it. And you have to share with each other. Rice is not only for you or for him. It is for everyone. Do you understand?"

The kitten was alone and scared. It cried and cried. It wanted to be loved and fed and warm. But no one came. The night was cold and dark. The kitten was too weak and sick to survive. It died in the box.

The moral of the story is: Don't take things that don't belong to you. Don't act without thinking of the consequences. Don't ignore the needs and feelings of others. Be kind and respectful to all living things.

She pulled the blanket over the metal frame and made a cozy tent. She crawled inside with her doll and her book. She pretended she was camping in the woods. She read stories to her doll and gave her water from a cup. She was having a lot of fun.

But she did not know that the metal frame was getting hotter and hotter from the sun. The blanket trapped the heat inside the tent. Lily started to feel very warm and uncomfortable. She said to her doll, "It's too hot in here. Let's go outside."

She tried to push the blanket away, but it was stuck to the metal. She pulled harder, but it did not move. She felt scared and trapped. She cried out, "Help! Help! I can't get out!"

Her mom heard her cry and ran to her room. She saw the tent and smelled the smoke. She quickly grabbed the blanket and pulled it off the metal. She saw Lily and her doll, red and sweaty. She hugged them and said, "Oh, Lily, are you okay? You should never polish your bed on a hot day. The metal can burn you and the blanket can catch fire. That's very dangerous."

Lily nodded and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to play. I didn't know it would get so hot."

Her mom kissed her and said, "It's okay, honey. I'm glad you're safe. Next time, let's play in the shade or inside the house. And let's get you some ice cream to cool you down."

Lily smiled and said, "Okay, mom. I love you. And I love my bed. But I don't want to polish it anymore."

Tom felt angry and hurt. He did not like that Sam laughed at him. He wished he had his cone back. He looked at the dog and saw that it had finished the cone and was looking for more. He had an idea.

"Hey, Sam, look at that ancient house over there," Tom said.

Sam looked at the house. It was old and broken. He did not see why Tom wanted him to look at it. He did not see that Tom was holding his cone too high. The bird that Tom had pointed at before flew down and grabbed Sam's cone from his hand. Sam was shocked and sad. He started to cry.

"Hey, that's not fair!" Sam said. "That bird took my cone!"

Tom saw what happened and laughed. He thought it was funny that Sam lost his cone. He did not share his cone with Sam. He just licked his cone and said, "Too bad for you, Sam. You should have been more careful."

Sam felt angry and hurt. He did not like that Tom laughed at him. He wished he had his cone back. He looked at Tom and saw that he had a big smile on his face. He realized that Tom had tricked him.

"Tom, you are mean!" Sam said. "You made the bird take my cone!"

Tom shrugged and said, "You laughed at me first. You deserved it."

Sam and Tom glared at each other. They did not talk to each other. They did not play with each other. They did not have fun.

The man in the truck saw what happened. He felt sorry for the boys. He decided to give them another chance. He called them over and said, "Boys, I have two more cones for you. But this time, you have to promise me something. You have to promise me that you will not laugh at each other. You have to promise me that you will share your cones. You have to promise me that you will be kind to each other. Can you do that?"

Sam and Tom looked at each other. They felt ashamed. They knew they had been wrong. They nodded and said, "Yes, sir. We promise."

The man in the truck smiled and gave them two more cones, one strawberry and one mint. He said, "Good. Now, go and enjoy your ice cream, and remember to be nice to each other."

Sam and Tom thanked the man and walked away with their cones. They were very happy and licked their ice cream. They did not drop their cones. They did not laugh at each other. They shared their cones. They were kind to each other. They had fun.

The moral of the story is: Do not laugh at others when they are sad. Share what you have with others. Be kind to others. You will be happier that way.

He saw a small hole in the cage. He thought, maybe I can escape through the hole. He tried to squeeze his body and his wings through the hole, but it was too tight. He felt sad and scared.

Then he heard a voice. It was a girl who came to look at the bird. She said, "Hello, bird. You are so pretty. What is your name?" The bird did not know how to talk to the girl, but he made a sound. He said, "Tweet, tweet."

The girl smiled. She said, "Tweet, tweet. That is a nice name. Do you like your cage?" The bird shook his head. He said, "No, no. I want to go home. I want to fly."

The girl felt sorry for the bird. She said, "I understand. You are not happy here. I will help you." She looked around and saw no one was watching. She opened the cage door and said, "Go, tweet, tweet. Go and find your home."

The bird was surprised and happy. He said, "Thank you, thank you. You are kind. You are my friend." He flew out of the cage and into the sky. He felt free and glad. Then he sees a boy with a shirt he likes. The shirt has a picture of a truck on it. Sam likes trucks. He wants to touch the shirt and the truck. He runs to the boy and says "truck, truck". He reaches out his hand to touch the shirt.

But the boy does not like that. He does not want Sam to touch his shirt. He says "no, no, go away". He pushes Sam away. Sam falls down and hurts his knee. He cries.

His mom comes and hugs him. She says "I'm sorry, Sam. You can't touch other people's shirts without asking. That is not good. That is rude. You have to say please and thank you. You have to be nice and polite. Do you understand?"

Sam nods. He is sad and sorry. He says "sorry, mom. Sorry, boy. Please, can I touch your shirt? Thank you." He hopes the boy will be nice and let him touch his shirt. He hopes the boy will be his friend. He hopes he can learn more words. He hopes he can have a good day.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to run and jump and chase each other. They had a lot of fun, but they also got very tired.

"Let's rest for a bit," Lily said. "We can sit under the big tree and have some water."

"OK," Tom agreed. They ran to the tree and sat down. They drank some water from their bottles and felt better.

But then they heard a loud noise. It was their dog, Spot. He had found a hole in the fence and had escaped. He was barking and running in the street.

"Oh no, Spot!" Tom and Lily shouted. "He might get lost or hurt. We have to get him back."

They got up and ran after Spot. They called his name and tried to catch him. But Spot was too fast and too excited. He did not listen to them.

They saw a man walking on the sidewalk. He had a kind face and a big hat. He saw Spot and stopped.

"Hello, little dog," he said. "Are you lost? Where is your home?"

He bent down and petted Spot. Spot liked him and licked his hand.

"Please, mister, can you help us?" Tom and Lily asked. "That's our dog, Spot. He escaped from our garden. We need to take him back."

The man looked at them and smiled. He was honest and good.

"Of course, I can help you," he said. "I love dogs. Here, take this leash and put it on Spot. Then you can walk him back to your garden. Be careful and stay on the sidewalk."

He gave them a leash and helped them put it on Spot. Spot calmed down and wagged his tail.

"Thank you, mister," Tom and Lily said. "You are very nice."

"You're welcome, kids," the man said. "And you are very brave and honest. Take good care of Spot. He is a lucky dog to have you."

Tom and Lily nodded and thanked him again. They walked Spot back to their garden. They fixed the hole in the fence and gave Spot some food and water. They hugged him and told him they loved him.

Then they rested under the big tree and smiled. They were happy and safe. They had a good day.

One day, they decided to have a poppy contest. They wanted to see who could make the most beautiful poppy crown. They opened the box and started to choose the poppies they liked. Lily was very organized. She sorted the poppies by color and size. She made a plan in her head of how to arrange them. Max was not organized. He grabbed the poppies at random and threw them on the ground. He did not have a plan. He just wanted to finish quickly.

"Look, Lily, I'm done!" Max said, holding his poppy crown. It was messy and uneven. Some poppies were falling off. Some poppies were upside down. "How about you?"

Lily looked at her poppy crown. It was neat and symmetrical. She had used different colors and shapes to make a pattern. She was proud of her work. "I'm done, too," she said, holding her poppy crown.

They showed their poppy crowns to their mom, who was watching them from the window. She smiled and praised them both. "You both did a great job," she said. "But I have a surprise for you. Come with me."

She led them to the other side of the garden, where there was a big tree. Under the tree, there was a picnic basket and a blanket. "I made some sandwiches and cookies for you," she said. "But you have to choose one thing to share with each other. What will it be?"

Lily and Max looked at the basket. There were many yummy things inside. They both wanted the cookies, but there were only two. They looked at each other and remembered their poppy crowns. Lily thought of how Max had not been organized and how his poppy crown had looked. Max thought of how Lily had been organized and how her poppy crown had looked. They both felt sorry for each other.

Lily reached for the cookies and gave one to Max. "Here, you can have this," she said. "You worked hard on your poppy crown."

Max reached for the sandwiches and gave one to Lily. "Here, you can have this," he said. "You made a beautiful poppy crown."

They hugged and thanked each other. They ate their sandwiches and cookies and enjoyed the picnic. They learned that being organized was good, but being kind was better. They also learned that sharing was fun, and that poppies were more than just pretty flowers. They were also symbols of love and friendship.

Lily felt proud of herself for helping her friend. They continued to play in the pool, but this time, they were more careful. They knew that the pool could be dangerous if they weren't careful.

"OK, but be careful. It might be prickly," Lily said.

They walked to the hedge and looked for a gap. They found one and squeezed through. Behind the hedge, they saw a small pond with some ducks and frogs.

"Wow, look at the animals!" Sam said.

He ran to the pond and tried to touch a duck. The duck quacked and splashed water at him. Sam laughed and got wet.

Lily followed him and saw a frog on a rock. She reached out to touch the frog. The frog jumped and landed on her head. Lily screamed and shook her head. The frog hopped off and croaked.

They both laughed and looked at each other. They were wet and dirty, but they had fun.

"Let's go back to the hedge before Mom and Dad see us," Sam said.

"OK, but don't tell them about the pond. It's our secret," Lily said.

They ran back to the hedge and crawled through. They wiped their clothes and hair and pretended nothing happened. They joined Mom and Dad on the bench and smiled.

"Did you have a good time, kids?" Mom asked.

"Yes, we did. We played a lot," Sam said.

"What did you play?" Dad asked.

"We played... touch the hedge," Lily said.

Mom and Dad looked at each other and smiled. They knew the kids were hiding something, but they didn't mind. They were happy to see them happy.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play ball in the park. They have a big ball and a small bat. They take turns to hit the ball and run.

One day, they see a man and a boy in the park. The man has a big glove and a big bat. The boy has a small glove and a small ball. The man throws the ball to the boy. The boy tries to hit the ball with the bat.

Tim and Sam watch them. They want to play with them. They go near them and say hello.

"Hello, can we play with you?" Tim asks.

"Sure, why not?" the man says. "I'm Dan and this is my son, Ben. What are your names?"

"I'm Tim and this is Sam," Tim says.

"Nice to meet you, Tim and Sam," Dan says. "Do you want to try to hit the ball?"

"Yes, please," Sam says.

"OK, Sam, you go first. Ben, you throw the ball to Sam. Tim, you watch and learn," Dan says.

Ben takes the small ball and goes to the pitch. The pitch is a place where you throw the ball. He stands far from Sam. He holds the ball in his hand. He swings his arm and throws the ball to Sam.

Sam holds the small bat in his hand. He watches the ball. He swings the bat and tries to hit the ball. But the ball is too fast and too small. He misses the ball.

"Strike one!" Dan says.

Sam tries again. Ben throws the ball again. Sam swings the bat again. But the ball is too high and too far. He misses the ball again.

"Strike two!" Dan says.

Sam tries one more time. Ben throws the ball one more time. Sam swings the bat one more time. But the ball is too low and too close. He misses the ball again.

"Strike three! You're out!" Dan says.

Sam is sad. He gives the bat to Tim. He goes to the side and sits on the grass.

"Good try, Sam. Don't worry, it's hard to hit the ball. You'll get better with practice," Dan says.

"Thank you, Dan. Can I try again later?" Sam asks.

"Of course, Sam. You can try again later. Now it's Tim's turn. Let's see what he can do," Dan says.

Tim takes the small bat and goes to the pitch. He is nervous. He hopes he can hit the ball. He watches Ben. Ben takes the small ball and goes to the pitch. He stands far from Tim. He holds the ball in his hand. He swings his arm and throws the ball to Tim.

Tim watches the ball. He sees the ball is thick. The ball is not small like Ben's ball. The ball is big like Tim's ball. Tim smiles. He likes big balls. He thinks he can hit the ball. He swings the bat and hits the ball.

The ball flies in the air. It goes over Ben's head. It goes over Dan's head. It goes over the trees. It goes out of the park.

"Wow! What a hit! You hit a home run, Tim!" Dan says.

Tim is happy. He runs around the pitch. He jumps and cheers. He goes to Dan and Ben and gives them high fives.

"Thank you, Dan. Thank you, Ben. That was fun. Can we play again?" Tim asks.

"Sure, Tim. You're a great hitter. We can play again. But first, let's go and find the ball. It's a good ball. It's a thick ball. It's a magic ball," Dan says.

They all laugh and run to find the ball. They have a good time. They are friends. They like to play ball in the park.

"Look, Dad, look!" Lily cried. "What is that?"

"Yeah, Dad, that was cool!" Lily agreed.

Dad smiled and kissed them. "I'm glad you liked it, kids. The port is full of wonders. Come on, let's see what else we can find."

They saw a stall with bright red apples. They looked so juicy and sweet. Tom and Lily ran towards the stall, but their mom and dad caught them by the hand. They said "No, you have to resist. You can't just take things that are not yours. You have to ask and pay first."

Tom and Lily tried to pull away, but their mom and dad were stronger. They said "Sorry" to the lady who was selling the apples. She smiled and said "It's okay. They are very curious and hungry. Here, you can have one apple each, as a gift. But you have to promise to stay on the path and listen to your mom and dad."

Tom and Lily nodded and said "Thank you". They took the apples and bit into them. They were so tasty and crunchy. They felt happy and sorry at the same time. They learned that they had to resist their impulses and follow the rules. They also learned that sometimes, kindness can make things better. Tommy and Anna were playing in the garden. They saw a rabbit hopping around. They wanted to catch it and pet it.

"Come here, bunny!" Tommy said. He ran after the rabbit. Anna followed him.

But the rabbit was fast and clever. It ran into a hole under a big tree. Tommy and Anna could not see it anymore.

"Where did it go?" Anna asked. She was sad.

"Maybe it is hiding," Tommy said. He looked around. He saw a big pile of carrots near the hole. "Look, Anna! Carrots! Maybe the rabbit likes them. Let's give some to the rabbit. Maybe it will come out."

Tommy and Anna picked up some carrots and put them near the hole. They waited for the rabbit to come out. But nothing happened.

They picked up more carrots and put them near the hole. They waited some more. But still nothing happened.

They picked up all the carrots and put them near the hole. They waited and waited. But the rabbit did not come out.

They were confused. Why did the rabbit not want the carrots? They had given it so many.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. They turned around and saw a big, fat, orange cat. It had a mysterious smile on its face. It had eaten all the carrots!

"Meow!" the cat said. It licked its lips. It looked at Tommy and Anna. It looked hungry.

Tommy and Anna were scared. They ran away from the cat. They ran back to their house. They locked the door.

They learned a lesson. They learned that they should not try to catch a rabbit that does not want to be caught. They learned that they should not leave food outside for a mysterious cat. They learned that they should be careful in the garden.

Bob walked closer to the house and as he got nearer he could hear a voice shouting. He clambered over the fence and peered inside the house. To his surprise, he saw a little girl who was looking very upset. She was running back and forth, pointing to her bedroom.

Bob crept into the house and asked the girl why she was so upset. She told him that something had appeared in her bedroom and she was scared of it. Bob put his paw on her shoulder and said, "Don't worry, I will help you find out what it is." 

Bob and the girl crept into her bedroom together. There, standing in the corner was a tiny mouse. Bob laughed and said, "Don't be scared, the mouse won't hurt you." The girl smiled and thanked Bob for helping her.

From then on, Bob visited the little girl every day and they became best friends. He always made sure to check her room for any surprises!

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong bear who was very thoughtful. One day, he wanted to go for a swim in a nearby lake. He gathered his things and entered the lake. Suddenly, a loud voice shouted, "Hey bear! Stop right there!" 

The bear looked around and saw a tiny farmer standing at the edge of the lake. He held an axe in his hands and said, "I'm sorry, bear, but you can't swim here. It's my lake, and I won't let you in." 

The bear was confused but he tried to be polite. "I'm sorry, sir," he said. "I didn't know this was your lake. Is there somewhere else I can go to swim?" 

The farmer thought for a moment and then shook his head. "No. No, I'm afraid not. You need to leave now," he said sternly. 

The bear sighed and walked back to the shore. Suddenly, the farmer swung the axe and hit the bear hard in the back. "That's for entering my lake!" he shouted. The bear felt a sharp pain and fell to the ground. 

And that's the end of the story. The poor bear never got a chance to go for a swim in the lake. He had been so thoughtful, but the farmer was too mean.

But the metal box didn't move. It was so tidy that it stayed in the same spot. It lay on its side, still red and shiny.

A little girl came around the corner. She saw the metal box and smiled. She went over and picked it up, puts it in its original spot and put the lid back on top. 

The little girl and the metal box were both very happy. That's how the box stopped falling and stayed tidy!
