"Look, Mia, this is a microscope. We can see bugs and leaves and other things with it," Tom says.

Mia is curious. She wants to try the microscope. But Tom is impatient. He does not want to share his toy.

"No, Mia, this is mine. You can play with something else," he says.

Mia is sad. She does not like it when Tom is mean. She looks around and sees a book on the shelf. It is a book about animals.

"Mia, why don't you suggest a game we can play with the book?" her mom says. She knows Mia likes animals.

Mia thinks for a moment. Then she has an idea.

"OK, mom, I have a game. Tom, do you want to play with me?" she asks.

Tom is bored with the microscope. He nods.

"What is the game?" he asks.

Mia smiles. She opens the book and points to a picture of a lion.

"The game is called 'Guess the Animal'. I will show you a picture of an animal, and you have to guess what it is. If you guess right, you get a point. If you guess wrong, I get a point. The one with the most points wins," she explains.

Tom likes the game. He thinks he knows a lot of animals.

"OK, let's play. I will go first. What is this?" he says, and shows Mia a picture of a zebra.

Mia looks at the picture. She knows what it is.

"That is a zebra. It has black and white stripes," she says.

"OK, you are right. You get a point. Now it is your turn. Show me an animal," he says.

Mia flips the page and finds a picture of a penguin.

"What is this?" she asks.

Tom looks at the picture. He does not know what it is.

"Is it a duck?" he guesses.

Mia laughs.

"No, it is not a duck. It is a penguin. It lives in the cold and swims in the water," she says.

Mia gets another point. She is happy. Tom is not.

"Yay, I won! I have ten points. You have five points," she says.

Tom is sad. He does not like to lose.

"Your game is not fair. You have an easy book. My microscope is better," he says.

Mia does not want to fight with Tom. She wants to be nice.

She ran to the door and called Amy to come over. She told her about the gift and how she wanted to play with her. Amy was surprised and delighted. She thanked Lily and hugged her. They opened the box and found a beautiful dollhouse with many accessories. They played together for hours, laughing and having fun.

Lily learned that being spoiled is not good and that sharing is caring. She also learned that having a friend is more valuable than having many things. She was happy and grateful for her dream, her parents and her gift. She never threw tantrums again.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play together. One day, they went to the store with their moms. They saw many things that they wanted, like toys and candy. But their moms said they only had money for food and clothes.

Lily saw a shiny necklace that looked like a star. She wanted it very much, but she knew she had no money. She looked around and saw that no one was watching. She put the necklace in her pocket and smiled.

Ben saw what Lily did and felt sad. He knew that taking things without paying was wrong. He wanted to tell Lily to put the necklace back, but he was afraid she would be angry with him. He kept quiet and followed his mom.

On their way home, they passed by a temple. Lily and Ben saw people praying and giving thanks. Lily felt something in her pocket and remembered the necklace. She felt bad and scared. She wondered if God saw what she did and if he was angry with her.

She whispered to Ben, "I did something bad. I took a necklace from the store without paying. I'm sorry. What should I do?"

Ben was glad that Lily told him the truth. He said, "You should be honest and give it back. Maybe the store owner will forgive you. And maybe God will too. Come on, I'll go with you."

Lily nodded and took out the necklace. She and Ben ran back to the store and found the owner. Lily gave him the necklace and said, "I'm sorry, sir. I took this without paying. I was wrong. Please forgive me."

The owner looked at Lily and Ben. He saw that they were sorry and brave. He said, "Thank you for being honest and returning the necklace. I forgive you. But don't do it again. Stealing is bad and hurts others. Honesty is good and makes others happy."

Lily and Ben felt relieved and happy. They thanked the owner and left. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that honesty is the best policy.

One day, their mom and dad told them they were going on a vacation. They were very happy and excited. They packed their bags and got in the car. They learned that vacation is not only about having fun, but also about being with family.

Ben and Mia put on their swim suits and ran to the water. They splashed and laughed and kicked their feet. They saw some fish and crabs and starfish. They were very happy.

Mia heard Ben and looked at the water. She saw the shark too. She was scared and grabbed Ben's hand. They ran to the shore as fast as they could.

Mom and Dad saw Ben and Mia running and heard them yelling. They ran to them and hugged them. They asked them what was wrong.

Ben and Mia told them about the shark. They pointed to the water. Mom and Dad looked at the water. They saw the shark too. But they did not look scared. They looked calm.

Mom and Dad said, "That is not a shark. That is a dolphin. Dolphins are friendly and smart. They like to play and jump. They do not hurt people. They live in the reef, where there are many other animals and plants."

Mom and Dad said, "Yes, but be careful and stay close to us."

Soon, the popcorn started to pop. It popped so loud and fast that Sara got scared. She ran away from the stove and hid behind the couch. The popcorn kept popping and popping. It filled the pot and spilled over. It flew out of the pot and landed on the floor, the table, the chairs, the windows. It made a big mess.

Sara's mom came home and saw the popcorn everywhere. She was very angry. She turned off the stove and looked for Sara. She found her behind the couch, lying with her teddy bear. Sara was crying. She said she was sorry. She said she wanted to make popcorn for her mom.

Sara's mom hugged her and said it was okay. She said she was glad Sara was not hurt. She said popcorn was delicate and needed oil and butter and a lid. Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big tree with many birds. They wanted to see the birds up close, so they climbed the tree carefully.

"Look, Anna, there is a nest!" Ben said, pointing to a small bowl of sticks and feathers. "It has four eggs inside. They are blue and speckled."

Once there was a little girl called Debbie. Debbie loved cherries very much. She used to pick them from the tree in her garden every day. 

One afternoon, Debbie was helping her mom in the kitchen. She saw her mom pouring cherries into a bowl. "What are you doing, mom?" Debbie asked. 

Her mom smiled and told her, "I'm making a cherry pie. It's going to be delicious!"

One of the youths replied with a smile that they were here to find the secret to eternal happiness. The old man recommended that the group should search through some nearby caves. 

The youths eagerly agreed and set off. The young man thought hard, and replied that the secret to happiness was to stay kind and keep warm in cold weather. 

The youths thanked him, and then continued on their adventure. As they left, the old man whispered to the young man, telling him that he was wise beyond his years. 

The young man smiled, feeling very proud. As he finished sledding down the icy hills, he felt certain that he had found the real secret to eternal happiness.

One day, two police officers went to a house. They were careful as they walked in. Inside the house, they found a child, who was painting pictures. The child was using bright colors and had made some beautiful pictures. 

The police officers looked closely and smiled. They said, "That's very nice!" and the child smiled back. After that, the police officers took the child outside to show them a very special park. In the park, they saw even more colors. 

The police officers asked the child to choose their favorite color, and the child chose blue. So, the police officers and the child painted a big blue tree in the park. When they finished, everyone clapped and cheered. 

The police officers said, "That was very careful work!" and the child smiled with pride. Then, the police officers gave the child a special badge for doing such a good job and for being so careful. 

The child put the badge in their pocket and vowed to always be careful with their paint. The police officers nodded and said goodbye. The adventure was over - but the important lesson to be careful would stay with the child forever.

Once upon a time there was a small boy who loved to go on adventures. He wanted to see beyond the countryside near his home.

One day he decided he would find somewhere new. He put on his vest and bravely set off. But as he ventured further and further away, he realised he had no idea where he was going. He grew more and more helpless. 

The boy started to cry with frustration. Suddenly he heard a voice nearby. It was a kind old man.

The man said, "Why are you crying, my child?"

The boy said, "I don't know which way to go".

The man replied, "Let me help you. Follow me, and I'll show you the way".

And so the boy followed the kind old man. After a long journey, he found that he had returned to his home village.

The boy thanked the old man for his kind help and said, "There's no place like home".

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Jill.
Jack was feeling a bit sad because he had no power. All day, Jill was bossy and kept telling him what to do.
Jack got an idea. He smiled at Jill and asked if she wanted to play. She smiled back and nodded her head.
Jack wanted to offer her a game. He said, "Let's play the power game. I'll give you the power and you can tell me what to do."
Jill smiled, "Okay," and Jack gave her the power.
Jill was so happy with the power. She ran around and told Jack what to do. She even gave Jack special jobs. 
At the end of the day, they both had lots of fun. They offered each other a big hug and vowed to play the power game again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a big green hill. On top of it there was a patch of grass. It was so soft and smooth just like velvet.

One day, a little boy was curious to know what was on the top of the hill. When he reached the summit, he realized the grass was in bad condition. It was very dry and started to rot.

He asked a wise old man who was nearby, "What is wrong with the grass?"

"It is unknown" replied the wise old man. "It has been like this for a long time now."

The little boy was very sad to see that the grass was rotting but he knew there was nothing he could do. He decided to leave the hill and go back home.

Unfortunately, the story did not have a happy ending. The grass kept rotting and eventually it disappeared forever, leaving only an unknown memory of a once beautiful hill.

Once upon a time there was a man whose job was to count at an airport. Every day he sat there, counting and counting. But sometimes he noticed a smelly smell. It was coming from outside the airport. One day, the man decided to find out what caused the smelly smell.

He went outside the airport and saw a big smelly trash can. Inside the trash can were lots of egg shells, old food and lots of other smelly things. The man quickly put a lid on the trash can and some soap in it.

The next day when he went back to the airport, the man was happy to see the smelly smell was gone. He continued counting and counting happily until his job was done.

John woke with a big smile. His aunt was visiting today! He loved her so much, she was always so kind to him and gave him lots of hugs. She always brought him special treats that he loved.

John quickly put on his best shirt, took his Dad's hand and ran downstairs. When Auntie arrived, John couldn't help but grin. She was beautiful and full of love.

"Auntie! Hi!" John said with a beaming smile. She smiled right back and gave him a big hug. Then she showed him behind her back. What was it? John's eyes grew wide.

"It's a kite!" she said. "Let's go out and fly it together!"

John thanked his aunt over and over as they ran out to the yard. Finally, after a long day of flying the kite and enjoying the beautiful day, John said the biggest thank you of all. 

"Come back soon, Auntie," he said as he gave her one last hug. 

"I will," she said with a twinkle in her eye. "I'll see you again soon." And with that, John knew he would have another wonderful day with his aunt in the not too distant future.

Mama and Baby Bear were out for a walk together. They were looking for a nice spot to stop and rest so Mama could read a book. It didn't take them long before they found a perfect spot. There was a big tight rug in a sunny spot.

"Let's sit here," Mama said.

Baby Bear smiled and she eagerly jumped onto the rug. She curled up into a little ball, feeling comfortable and snug.

Mama opened up the book and started to read. And soon Baby Bear started to listen and enjoy the story too.

Time flew by and soon it was late.

"Time to go home," Mama said, closing the book.

Baby Bear reluctantly got up from the rug. She was sad to leave the spot where she had enjoyed the story so much. But she was looking forward to the next time that she and Mama could come back and sit on the rug again.

Lily felt sad and scared. She did not like to see her mom worried. She did not like to see the cars and trucks and buses that did not move. She did not like to wait and wait and wait. She wanted to see her grandma now.

She looked out the window and saw a boy on a bike. He was riding fast and weaving through the traffic. He had a big backpack on his back. He looked happy and free. Lily wished she had a bike like him. She said, "Mom, can we get out of the car and ride a bike to the hospital? It would be faster and more fun."

Lily's mom shook her head. She said, "No, sweetie, we can't do that. It's too dangerous. We have to stay in the car and be patient. We will get to the hospital soon. I'm sure grandma is waiting for us."

Lily sighed. She did not understand why they had to stay in the car and be patient. She thought riding a bike would be better. She felt angry and bored. She crossed her arms and pouted.

But then she remembered something. She remembered that her grandma always told her to be kind and grateful. She remembered that her grandma always gave her hugs and kisses and cookies. She remembered that her grandma always said, "I love you, Lily."

Lily felt a warm feeling in her heart. She realized that her mom was trying to do the best for her and her grandma. She realized that being angry and bored would not help anyone. She realized that being kind and grateful would make her and her mom and her grandma happy.

She smiled and said, "Mom, I'm sorry for being grumpy. I know you are doing your best. I love you, mom. And I love grandma, too. Can we call her and tell her that we are on our way?"

Lily's mom smiled back and said, "Of course, sweetie. That's a great idea. Let's call her and tell her that we love her and that we can't wait to give her a hug."

They called grandma and heard her voice. She sounded weak but happy. She said, "I love you, Lily. I love you, mom. I'm so glad you are coming. I can't wait to see you and give you a hug."

Lily and her mom felt a surge of joy and hope. They said, "We love you, grandma. We are almost there. We can't wait to see you and give you a hug, too."

They hung up the phone and held hands. They looked at the traffic and saw that it was moving again. They said, "Hooray! We are going to make it!"

They drove to the hospital and parked the car. They ran to the entrance and asked for grandma's room. They found her lying on a bed, surrounded by flowers and cards. She looked pale but happy. She saw them and smiled.

They ran to her and gave her a big hug. They said, "We are here, grandma. We are here. We love you so much."

Grandma hugged them back and said, "I'm so happy to see you. I love you so much, too. You are the best gift I could ever have."

They stayed with her and talked and laughed and cried. They felt a bond of love and gratitude that nothing could break. They learned that being kind and grateful is more important than being popular or fast or fun. They learned that being patient and hopeful is more powerful than being angry or bored or scared. They learned that giving and receiving hugs is the best way to heal and comfort. They learned that love is the most precious thing in the world.

One day, they saw a big vehicle on the road. It was red and shiny and had a loud siren. Tom and Lily wanted to see it better, so they ran towards the road.

Their mom came and hugged them. She was glad that they were safe. She told them that the fire truck was going to help someone who had a fire in their house. She said that fire trucks were good vehicles, but they had to be careful around them.

Tom and Lily nodded and said sorry to their mom. They went back to the park and played with their ball. They still liked to look at the fire truck, but they stayed far away from the road. They learned to be careful with dangerous vehicles.

Sara did not believe her mom. She did not think they would be happy in the new house. She did not want to go. She packed her things in a box, but she left her favorite teddy bear on the bed. She hoped someone would find it and love it.

When Timmy got home, his mom saw his smelly pants and knew right away what had happened. She took off his pants and put them in the wash. Timmy felt sad because he loved those pants, but he was happy that his mom could clean them and make them smell nice again.

From that day on, Timmy always listened to his mom and was careful not to slip on the wet ground. He also learned that it was important to take care of his clothes, especially when they got smelly or dirty.

Once upon a time, there was a monkey. He was very happy swinging from tree to tree. One day, he ate a magic banana and started to shrink! The monkey became very small and had to be patient while waiting for the magic to wear off. 

The monkey was so tiny that he could fit in the palm of your hand. He was scared but he knew he had to be patient. He waited and waited until finally, he started to grow again. The monkey was so happy to be his normal size again. He swung from tree to tree, feeling grateful that he was no longer tiny. 

From that day on, the monkey never ate another magic banana again. He learned that sometimes it's better to be patient and wait for things to happen naturally. And he was happy to be a regular-sized monkey once again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little crab named Coco. Coco lived on a reef with many other sea creatures. Coco had a hairy shell that made her look very cute.

One day, Coco was playing hide and seek with her friends. She found a big shell and decided to hide under it. Suddenly, she heard a loud noise. It was her friend, Sammy the starfish. "Coco, come quick! The tide is coming and we need to cover ourselves!" said Sammy.

Coco quickly crawled out from under the shell and saw that the water was rising. She and her friends worked together to cover themselves with seaweed and rocks so they wouldn't get swept away. They were all safe and happy, thanks to their teamwork.

When they arrived at the park, Lily ran to the playground and forgot about the bird. But as they were eating their sandwiches, Lily saw something in the tree. It was the rare bird her mom told her about! Lily was so happy and couldn't believe it was true. She felt like a special adventurer who discovered something amazing. From that day on, Lily always kept her eyes open for rare things because she knew anything can happen.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and go on adventures outside. One day, she went to visit her grandma who was very wise. Grandma had lots of wisdom and always knew what to do when Lily had a problem.

Lily didn't understand why some kids at school were being foolish and not sharing their toys. Grandma explained that sometimes people don't know how to be kind and that it's important to be patient and show them how to be nice. Lily listened carefully and decided to share her toys with the other kids.

From that day on, Lily learned the wisdom of being kind and patient. She realized that being foolish and not sharing was not the way to make friends. And so, she lived happily ever after with her new friends and her grandma's wisdom.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear named Bob. Bob was very tired and wanted to rest. He walked around the forest looking for a good spot to lie down. Suddenly, he saw a small rabbit hopping towards him.

"Hello Bob!" said the rabbit. "What are you doing?"

"I'm looking for a place to rest," replied Bob. "I'm very tired."

The rabbit looked up at Bob and said, "I know a good spot! Follow me!" Bob followed the rabbit to a big tree. The rabbit said, "You can rest here, Bob. The tree will protect you from the sun. Just be careful not to fall asleep for too long!"

"Thank you, rabbit," said Bob. "This spot is perfect. My eyes are heavy and I need to rest." Bob lay down and closed his eyes. He fell asleep quickly and dreamed of all the adventures he would have when he woke up.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, while they were playing, Lily's friend Sarah sneezed. "Bless you!" said Lily.

"Thanks," replied Sarah, wiping her nose with a tissue. "I have a rare allergy to pollen. It makes me sneeze a lot."

Lily didn't know what "rare" meant, but she knew that sneezing was no fun. She offered Sarah a tissue from her pocket and they continued playing. Later, they came to a cross in the path. They had to decide which way to go. "Let's go left," said Lily. "That way we can see the ducks in the pond."

"Okay," said Sarah, and they walked together towards the pond, holding hands. They had a great time feeding the ducks and playing in the sunshine. And even though Sarah sneezed a few more times, they didn't let it stop them from having fun.

Lily's mommy also told her that it's easy to gain friends by being kind and sharing. So, Lily went back to the park and shared her toys with her friends. Once upon a time, there was a little ant. The ant had to run very fast because it was late for a party. The ant knew it had to be dependable and arrive on time. 

But on the way to the party, the ant saw a big, scary spider. The spider was blocking the ant's path and the ant was very scared. It didn't want to get hurt or lose any of its inch-long legs.

Finally, the ant arrived at the party and everyone was so happy to see it. The ant felt proud of itself for being dependable and brave. And from that day on, the ant knew it could overcome any obstacle if it just kept running.

Fin was very happy and they played together every day. They liked to swim around the big coral reef and play hide-and-seek. One day, Otto said to Fin, "Let's play a game of match! We will try to find things that look the same." Fin thought this was a great idea and they started playing.

They found a shell that matched another shell, a rock that matched another rock, and finally, they found a net that matched another net. Fin was so happy to have a friend like Otto and he learned that sometimes, you just need to find the right match to make a friend.

Lila and Ben went to the park with Mom. They saw a pond with many ducks and swans. Lila liked the swans. They were white and big and lovely. She wanted to feed them some bread.

"Can I give them some bread, Mom?" Lila asked.

"Sure, but be careful. Don't go too close to the water. And don't touch the swans. They might bite you," Mom said.

Lila nodded and took a piece of bread from Mom. She walked to the edge of the pond and threw the bread to the swans. One swan came closer and ate the bread. Lila smiled and threw another piece.

Ben watched Lila and wanted to join her. He took a piece of bread from Mom and ran to the pond. He did not listen to Mom. He went too close to the water. He tried to touch the swan. The swan did not like that. It hissed and snapped at Ben.

Ben was scared and cried. He dropped the bread and ran back to Mom. Mom hugged him and said, "Are you okay, Ben?"

Ben nodded and said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I was bad. I did not listen to you. I tried to touch the swan. It was angry and hurt me."

Mom said, "It's okay, Ben. I'm glad you are not hurt. But you have to learn to be careful and respectful of the animals. They are not toys. They have feelings and needs. You have to treat them kindly and gently. Do you understand?"

Ben said, "Yes, Mom. I understand. I will be nice to the animals. I will not touch them. I will feed them from far away."

Mom said, "That's good, Ben. I'm proud of you. Now, let's go and join Lila. She is waiting for us."

They walked to Lila, who had paused to watch the swans. She saw Ben and said, "Hi, Ben. Do you want to feed the swans with me? They are lovely."

Ben said, "Yes, Lila. I want to feed the swans with you. They are lovely. But I will not touch them. I will be careful and respectful."

Lila said, "That's good, Ben. I'm happy you are here. Let's share the bread and have fun."

They fed the swans together and had fun. Mom watched them and smiled. She was happy they learned a lesson and enjoyed the park.

Lily and Sam liked to play in the snow. They put on their warm coats, hats, gloves and boots. They ran outside and saw the white snow everywhere. They made a big snowman with a carrot nose, a scarf and a hat. They gave him a smile and two eyes.

Then they saw a big pot on the porch. Mom had left it there for them. She said they could make snow soup. Lily and Sam thought that sounded fun. They took the pot and filled it with snow. They added some leaves, pine cones, berries and sticks. They pretended they were chefs and stirred the snow soup with a big spoon.

They tasted the snow soup. It was cold and crunchy and sweet and sour. They liked it. They made some more and put it in bowls. They invited the snowman to join them. They said, "Here, Mr. Snowman, have some snow soup. It is very good." They put a bowl in front of him and a spoon in his hand.

But the snowman did not eat. He did not move. He did not talk. He just stood there with his carrot nose, his scarf and his hat. Lily and Sam wondered why. They looked at him and saw that he was melting. The sun was shining and the snow was turning into water. They felt sad. They liked the snowman. They wanted him to stay.

They ran inside and told Mom. Mom hugged them and said, "Don't worry, my loves. The snowman will come back. He is just taking a long nap. When it snows again, he will wake up and you can play with him again. Snow soup will keep him happy until then." Lily and Sam smiled. They hoped it would snow soon. They wanted to see their snowman again. They loved him.

They run to the slide. But when they touch it, they feel heat. The slide is very hot. It hurts their hands.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Anna and Ben say.

They jump back. They look at the slide. It is in the sun. The sun makes the slide hot.

"Maybe we can wait for the slide to cool down," Anna says.

"Or maybe we can find something else to play with," Ben says.

They look around. They see a sandbox. There are many toys in the sandbox. There are buckets, shovels, cars, and animals. They see a cute teddy bear. It has a blue bow.

"Look! A teddy bear!" Anna says.

"I like teddy bears!" Ben says.

They run to the sandbox. They pick up the teddy bear. It is soft and fluffy. It does not hurt their hands.

"Can we share the teddy bear?" Anna asks.

"Sure! We can take turns," Ben says.

They hug the teddy bear. They smile. They are happy.

They forget about the slide. They play with the teddy bear and the other toys. They have fun in the sandbox.

Lily and Max are twins. They like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but their favorite ones are the puzzles. They like to match the pieces and make pictures.

One day, they are playing with a puzzle of a farm. Lily finds a piece with a cow. She looks for the piece with the cow's head. Max finds a piece with a pig. He looks for the piece with the pig's tail.

"Look, Lily, I have a pig!" Max says.

"Good, Max, but I have a cow!" Lily says.

They keep looking for the pieces. Lily finds the cow's head. She puts it next to the cow's body. She is happy. She has a cow.

Max finds the pig's tail. He puts it next to the pig's body. He is happy. He has a pig.

But then, Lily sees Max's pig. She wants it. She thinks it is better than her cow.

"Max, give me your pig!" Lily says. She is bossy.

"No, Lily, it is my pig!" Max says. He is angry.

They start to fight. They pull the puzzle pieces. They make a mess.

Their mom hears them. She comes to the room. She sees the mess. She is not happy.

"Stop, Lily and Max! What are you doing?" Mom says.

"Lily wants my pig!" Max says.

"Max has a better pig!" Lily says.

Mom sighs. She picks up the pieces. She puts them in the box.

"It is time for your meal. Come to the kitchen. You can play with the puzzle later. But you have to share and be nice. OK?" Mom says.

Lily and Max nod. They are hungry. They follow Mom to the kitchen. They hope Mom will make them something yummy. They hope they will have a good meal. They hope they will not fight again.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a large hill with a hole in it. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's go in the hole!" Lily said.

"OK, but be careful!" Ben said.

They crawled into the hole. It was dark and cold. They saw some bones on the ground.

"Look, a skeleton!" Lily said.

"Wow, it's so big!" Ben said.

They touched the bones. They felt hard and smooth.

"Hello, children," a voice said.

They looked up. They saw a large skeleton with a skull and teeth. It was smiling at them.

"Who are you?" Lily asked.

"I'm Mr. Bones. I live here. And you are?" the skeleton said.

"I'm Lily and this is Ben. We were playing in the park," Lily said.

"How nice. I'm glad you came to visit me. I don't get many visitors," the skeleton said.

"Can we go now?" Ben asked. He was scared.

"Go? But you just got here. And I'm so lonely. Why don't you stay with me?" the skeleton said.

He reached out his bony hands and grabbed Lily and Ben. They screamed and tried to get away, but the skeleton was too strong.

"Please, let us go!" Lily cried.

"No, no, no. You're my new friends. And friends don't leave each other. You'll stay with me forever," the skeleton said.

He dragged them deeper into the hole, where no one could hear them or find them. He laughed and said, "Now, let me introduce you to my other friends. They're all skeletons, too."

Lily liked to skip. She skipped to school, she skipped at playtime, she skipped all the way home. She was happy when she skipped, and she made a song in her head. "Skip, skip, skip, I love to skip, skip, skip, skip, it makes me feel so good!"

One day, she saw a group of kids on the playground. They were playing with a ball, and they looked like they were having fun. Lily wanted to join them, so she skipped over to them and said, "Hi, can I play with you?"

The kids looked at her and laughed. "No, you can't play with us," one of them said. "You're too silly. You always skip around like a baby. You don't know how to play with a ball. Go away!"

Lily felt sad and hurt. She didn't understand why they were so mean to her. She liked to skip, and she thought it was fun. She turned around and skipped away, but her song was gone.

She skipped to a bench and sat down. She felt like crying, but she didn't want anyone to see her. She wished she had a friend who liked to skip too.

Then, she heard a voice behind her. "Hi, can I sit with you?" It was a boy with curly hair and a big smile. He had a book in his hand.

Lily looked up and nodded. She moved over to make some room for him. He sat down and opened his book. "I'm Ben," he said. "I like to read. Reading makes me happy, and I learn a lot of things. What do you like to do?"

Lily smiled a little and said, "I like to skip. Skipping makes me happy, and I make a song in my head."

Ben nodded and said, "That's cool. Skipping is fun, and making a song is creative. You must be very wise."

Lily felt a warm feeling in her chest. She liked Ben. He was nice and he didn't laugh at her. He liked to read, and she liked to skip. They were different, but they were also the same. They both liked to do what made them happy, and they both wanted to learn.

They started to talk and share their book and their song. They became friends, and they skipped and read together. They were happy, and they didn't care what the other kids said. They knew they were wise.

Lily and Max were friends who liked to play with numbers. They had a big book with many numbers and pictures. Lily liked to count the numbers and Max liked to draw the pictures.

One day, they found a page with a big zero. Zero was a circle with nothing inside. Lily said, "Zero is a funny number. It means nothing. It is not like one, two, or three."

Max said, "Zero is not funny. It is important. It can make other numbers bigger. Like ten, or hundred, or thousand. Zero can also be in the middle. Like twenty, or fifty, or ninety."

Lily did not believe Max. She thought he was making things up. She said, "Zero is not important. It is silly. You are silly too. You do not know anything about numbers. You only know how to draw."

Max felt sad and angry. He did not like to be teased by Lily. He said, "You are mean. You do not know how to be a friend. You only know how to count. You think you are smarter than everyone."

They started to argue and shout. They did not want to play with each other anymore. They turned away and ignored each other.

They asked their parents if they could act in a movie, but their parents said no. They said acting was not easy and they were too young. They said they should focus on school and other activities. Tom and Anna were sad and angry. They thought their parents did not understand them.

They decided to act in a movie by themselves. They took a camera and some costumes and went to the park. They made up a story about a prince and a princess who lived in a small country. They wanted to be independent and free from a bad king. They acted out their story and recorded it on the camera.

They were very proud of their movie and showed it to their parents. They hoped their parents would like it and let them act more. But their parents were not happy. They said they were worried and upset. They said they should not have gone to the park without telling them. They said they could have gotten lost or hurt. They said they should not have taken the camera and the costumes without asking. They said they should not have lied to them.

Tom and Anna felt sorry and ashamed. They realized they had made a mistake. They apologized to their parents and gave them a hug. They said they understood their parents cared for them and wanted them to be safe and happy. They said they still liked acting, but they would not do it without their parents' permission. They said they would listen to their parents and respect their rules.

Their parents forgave them and smiled. They said they were proud of their creativity and talent. They said they would support their dreams, but they also wanted them to be responsible and honest. They said they would watch their movie together and give them some feedback. They said they loved them very much.

Tom and Anna learned a lesson that day. They learned that acting was fun, but not more important than their family and their safety. They learned that being independent did not mean being selfish or disobedient. They learned that being honest and respectful was the best way to act.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily lived in a small village surrounded by mountains. One day, she woke up and saw the fog outside. She looked out of the window and saw that everything was covered in a white mist. She said to her mom, "Mommy, look at the fog! It's so big!"

Her mom replied, "Yes, it is. We should be careful when we go outside."

Lily and her mom decided to go for a walk in the forest. They walked for a while until they came across a humble cottage. They knocked on the door and an old lady answered. She invited them in and they sat down to have some tea. The old lady looked at Lily and said, "You have such a kind heart. You will do great things one day."

Lily smiled and thanked the old lady. They finished their tea and said goodbye. As they walked back home, Lily gazed at the fog and said, "I wonder what adventures await me."

But as they got closer to their house, they saw that it was on fire. They tried to go inside to save their things, but the fire was too strong. They lost everything they had. Lily cried and said, "What will we do now?"

Her mom hugged her and said, "We will rebuild. We still have each other."

From that day on, Lily remembered what the old lady said to her and tried to be kind to everyone she met. She never forgot the humble cottage in the forest and the kind old lady who gave her hope.

One day, a little girl named Mia entered a big open field. There, she saw a huge cactus. Mia was so excited and ran right up to it. The cactus was so tall, she couldn't touch the top. She settled with looking at it from the base.

All of a sudden, a boy appeared from behind the cactus. His name was Jack, and he was very jealous of Mia's enthusiasm for the cactus. He wanted to be the one that first saw the cactus.

Jack made a mean face at Mia and said, "That's MY cactus!"

Mia didn't like how jealous he was and she said, "No! That's MY cactus!"

Jack was mad and wanted to prove that it was his so he said, "Race me up to the top, and whoever gets there first, gets to keep the cactus."

Mia accepted the challenge and they both ran up to the top of the cactus. Jack was fast, but Mia was faster! She reached the top first and won the race.

Mia was so proud of herself and Jack was so jealous! He knew that Mia was the one who would get to keep the cactus. But even though Mia won the race, she decided to share the cactus with Jack. They both smiled and enjoyed their special cactus together.

Once upon a time there was a humble cabbage farmer. Every day he weighed his cauliflowers and collected them in his truck. One day he put extra cauliflowers he had been given into his truck. When he weighed them he saw they were much heavier than his own. He thought to himself, "This must be a very special cauliflower".

He took the cauliflower to the market. Everyone who saw it was amazed. They said, "What a big and beautiful cauliflower, it must be worth so much money".
The farmer weighed the cauliflower and it weighed the most of any he had ever seen before. He was so excited he sold it for lots of money.

The farmer was very happy. With the money he bought more seeds for his farm, and lots of things for his family. He never forgot the humble cauliflower that had made his dreams come true.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He was very excited, because he was going on a safari. He put on his funny hat and everyone laughed. He said goodbye to his mom and they set off.

The boy was so excited! He saw so many interesting things on the safari. He saw elephants, zebras and giraffes.

The sun was getting low in the sky, so it was time to go home. The boy started to hurry. He wanted to see one last thing before it was time to go. He wanted to see the lions!

Suddenly, there they were! The boy was so excited to see them. He watched them for a while and then it was time to hurry home. The boy was so happy. He had a fun safari.

One day, there were two friends in the park. They were having fun. Suddenly, an angry man came up to them. He was big and his face was red. His mouth was open and he was shouting.

The two friends began to tremble. They looked at each other and were scared. They didn't know what to do. Suddenly, the angry man started to walk away. He was still shouting but he soon disappeared.

The two friends looked at each other and smiled. They were so happy that the angry man had gone away. They quickly ran off to continue playing in the park.

Jack and Jill went for a walk, and they were so excited to explore the world. Jack had on a pink shoe, and Jill had on a blue shoe. They both looked so perfect!

As they walked, they noticed a tree and they decided to rest there. They sat down next to the tree and enjoyed the view all around them. They watched the birds flying in the sky, and the bees buzzing around the flowers.

Jack and Jill felt so happy, and before long, they began to get sleepy. So, they rested their eyes for a little nap and soon both of them were sleeping soundly.

When they woke up, Jack and Jill were refreshed and ready to continue their walk. They smiled, put their previously perfect shoes back on, and then went off to explore.

Once there was a gifted little girl. Her name was Mia and she was only three years old. Mia loved going on adventures. One day her mother said that it was time to hurry home. Mia got worried. She knew that if she didn't hurry home her mom would be sad.

So Mia ran and she ran as fast as she could. She ran past the trees, hopped over the fence and hopped into a puddle. Soon Mia was almost back home. Suddenly her mom appeared. She had come to hurry Mia home. Mom was so happy to see that Mia was almost home.

Mia was so excited. She said goodbye to her friends and ran home with her mom. They hurried together home and arrived safely. Mia was so happy!

Once upon a time there was a cube that was very enormous. All the children wanted to play with the cube. One day something special happened. A little girl was playing with the cube and it started to move all around the room. Everyone was so excited and wanted to see what was going to happen next. Suddenly the cube started to grow bigger and bigger until it was bigger than all the children in the room. They were all so amazed. They had so much fun playing with the enormous cube. They all laughed and ran around the room chasing the cube. The cube was so much fun that the children wanted to play with it all the time.

Mum and Dad had a surprise. They smiled and said they were going on holiday. They had lots of bags to unpack.
Mum and Dad showed their little girl the bags. They showed her their new beach clothes, their lunch boxes and lollies. Inside two bags were special presents for the little girl. 
Mum and Dad showed her two big boxes. On the top of the boxes were big, thick pins. The pins said "Happy Holiday". 
Mum and Dad helped the little girl to unpack the boxes. Inside were two new dolls. One doll had long, curly hair and the other had thick, wavy hair. The little girl was so excited! She hugged her dolls tightly. 
Mum and Dad were very happy. They said the dolls were to remember their holiday forever.
